audits.the_argument: NG's leg side = sign(dip_imb_level) when |dip_imb_level| >= 0.15, fired on the lagging Kalshi mark. The support is measurement-shaped, not day-net-shaped: n_strong_oos 34 at rate_oos 1.0, a monotone strength gradient stated as 0.68 -> 0.84 -> 0.94 -> 0.93, and an S95 fingerprint pass over G3-G5 held legs. Confidence 0.87, the highest in this batch. It sits in the MECHANISM family because the support IS a measurement and the mechanism (aggressor flow overlaps the nascent leg, so a signed imbalance nowcasts the leg's side) is argued rather than assumed. I classify it here and then report that the measurement does not reproduce - which is a stronger result than any label, and is only available BECAUSE the support was a measurement.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: Yes, and it comes out the other way. I re-ran the play's own bar on the file the claim was computed from. Over 6,351 usable legs on 108 days, |dip|>=0.15 gives 2,459/3,697 = 0.665, not 1.0, and the claimed monotone RISE with strength is INVERTED on the corpus: 0.688 (>=0.10) / 0.665 (>=0.15) / 0.628 (>=0.20) / 0.575 (>=0.30). The signal degrades as it strengthens. The rate is also nowhere near 1.0 anywhere, so this is not an overlapping-window tautology artifact - it is a real result, and the era split below is the shape of it. The play's own declared weak day (1020, quoted as 7/12) reproduces honestly at 10/14 on my slice, which is evidence the record is written in good faith even where the headline is wrong.

audits.the_argument: Two claims stacked. (1) Monday is a BIG mover, size UP. (2) The side comes from a three-armed reaction read - FADE a gap that jumped with a mature swing to a fresh cum-extreme, EXTEND at a fresh turn, and with no material gap carry FRIDAY's side. The bigness claim is checkable and I checked it. The three arms are not: every evidence entry in the play is of the form 'date X moved +N, guessed +M' with an arm assigned afterward to explain it, across eight separate per-event blobs (g6, g7, g10, g11, s96_2, s97_2, s98_2, s101_6, s102_1). The arms were carved out of the outcome record rather than derived from an independently measured quantity - the play says so itself when it retires the G3-G5 'Monday reversals' as 'swing-state coincidences, not a weekday property'.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: For the bigness claim yes, and it comes out the other way. For the arms, largely no: with three arms and a free swing-state selector, every Monday lands in one of them by construction. The play does carry two genuine acts of discipline that argue against a blanket dismissal - it FORWARD-FAILED its own gap-size arm in writing (1020, 0118, 0125 all under-forecast), and its declined_evidence block refuses to bank g20 0601's R3 as forward evidence because the constructed chain was inverted there, which is a specialist catching a state defect being laundered into evidence.

audits.the_argument: An armed turn near a scheduled catalyst fires the session BEFORE the event when a continuous weather ramp is live, and waits for the event when it is not. The causal argument is genuine and stated - weather models are a continuous twice-daily information stream, so when live they own the timing and the discrete print only adds magnitude and liquidity. But the core support is a catalogue: '1110 exhausted -> 1111 +1580', '1118 armed -> 1119 +1930', '1203 front-run confirmed +1520', with the fired/waited arm assigned after the fact. There is no independent measurement anywhere in the corpus of the ramp-live condition against a front-run rate. This is the best-behaved OUTCOME_CREDITED play in the batch - it carries two live self-falsifications (G9 1204 forward-failed in its original form and was re-armed; G10 0108 established the forbidden polarity-flip form) - but its support is still a list of days that delivered.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: Partly, and the part that could is the good part. The G16 pair is a real discriminator test that traces exactly to the committed price file: 0401 (D-1 to a pre-priced +34 print) delivered -590 and 0402 round-tripped to -150 / day_move -130, against 0409 (not pre-priced, building surplus on the block's most active tape) which delivered -610 with NO round-trip. Had 0409 also round-tripped, the discriminator would have died on the spot. That is real. The core fired-vs-waited tally (n=3 fired, n=2 waited) is not - it is five days sorted into two bins after the outcome.

audits.condition_can_change_state: This is the play's real defect and it is worse than a degenerate bar. The trigger has TWO limbs. The calendar limb (a scheduled catalyst 1-3 sessions ahead, served as flow_calendar.days_to_next_eia_release) is live and splits days cleanly. The ramp-live limb has NO SERVED DEFINITION, and the two natural readings of the same served object disagree in SIGN on the same day (20260624: horizon-0 forecast_run_delta_cdd -0.011 vs h1 d_gw_cdd +0.787). Under the h1 reading it is a constant, positive 20/20 across two groups - it cannot gate. Under the level reading it is whatever the reader says. So the limb either cannot change state or changes state by reader choice, and the corpus contains one specialist doing both inside one block.
audits.falsifier: The play carries NO falsifier field, though its caveats name a decisive test in prose ('the decisive test is the next winter armed-turn near a print'). What it actually needs first is a SERVED DEFINITION of ramp-live - pick the quantity and the bar - because until then the condition is not falsifiable, only arguable. Once defined: front-runs under a live ramp must beat the base rate of the pre-print session, measured on the intraday window and not on the day net (this is the exact defect s103.6 had to retract on D's pre-print generator).

audits.the_argument: This entry is not a conditional rule and says so in its own call field: 'DESCRIPTOR grade - regime context, not a scored play.' status DESCRIPTOR, confidence 0.4, forward_evidence NONE, n=1 full instance self-declared, and it explicitly refuses to promote a band. It is a description of what G12 did after the dead-sponsor squeeze - the unwind retraces the full squeeze leg in two gap-led sessions to the pre-squeeze shelf, then bases - with the magnitudes inside the unwind derived as arithmetic (gap = -E, next session = remaining premium to the shelf). Classifying its support was the category error the corrected rubric was written to stop, so I say what it is and record what traces. WHAT TRACES EXACTLY: the two unwind sessions. WHAT DOES NOT: the nine-session basing band, which is wrong on the upside by 0.291 (about 2,900 dollars in day-move terms).
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: Not applicable as a support test - it is a descriptor. But two of its statements are checkable and I checked both: the unwind arithmetic reproduces to the tick, and the basing band does not reproduce at all. The S101.6 amendment is also a genuine act of scoping under pressure rather than tent-widening: when G13 broke the 3.159 shelf three weeks later, the claim was NARROWED to the unwind sessions themselves and the post-basing shelf was demoted to an ordinary reference level, rather than the descriptor being loosened to accommodate the break.

audits.the_argument: A Monday 06:00 ET L1-10 resting-book imbalance (|imb10| >= ~0.05) marks the caught/stacked side, and the 06-10 window leans AGAINST it as a tie-breaker under R3, never overriding it. A mechanism IS argued - Greg's weekend-carry read, modified by measurement to 06:00 rather than the Sunday reopen because the reopen book measured uninformative at 8/14. But the support is 'qualifying 6/7' on a subset selected at a bar chosen by the same refine pass that saw the outcomes: 7 of 14 Mondays were filtered out and the rate is quoted on what survived. On n=7 a 6/7 is roughly p=0.06 one-sided against a coin flip, and the play itself reports that the shallower L1-3 read gives 8/14 and that the window repricing runs against its own aggressor flow 8/14 - both coin flips. The play states its own remaining gap honestly: no Tue-Thu control run, so Monday-specificity is unproven.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: In principle yes, but I cannot put it to any test, because the underlying measurement is committed NOWHERE - so the play's headline cannot have come out the other way in any way anyone can check. THE FULL SEARCH RECORD, since d24_state is not_searched and I list ZERO instances rather than dressing stand-downs up as evidence. (1) git grep imb10 across the whole repo: hits ONLY in knowledge/ng_brain.json, its version backups, and BRAIN_AUDIT_PARTIAL_S111.json - zero hits anywhere in research/kalshi/forecasts/ or research/kalshi/renders/. (2) grep for imb10 and imb_R across research/kalshi/renders/ng_refine_s95/grp20_state.json through grp23_state.json: absent from all four. (3) research/kalshi/renders/ng_refine_s95/fingerprints.json, the only committed file carrying any book quantity at all: it holds a per-LEG imb_R at leg-entry time on L1-3 depth fields (bid_dep_entry / ask_dep_entry), which is the wrong depth AND the wrong timestamp for a Monday 06:00 L1-10 snapshot, and two of the seven named derivation Mondays (20251027, 20260309) are not in it at all. (4) research/kalshi/S102_MERGE_PROPOSAL.md lines 70-73 restate the 6/7, the L1-3 8/14 and the against-own-flow 8/14 in prose only - and per the instance discipline, prose citing prose is one instance, not two. (5) The four modern Mondays in research/kalshi/forecasts/g22_perday/grp22_B_20260622.json, research/kalshi/forecasts/g22_perday/grp22_B_20260629.json, research/kalshi/forecasts/g23_perday/grp23_B_20260706.json and research/kalshi/forecasts/g23_perday/grp23_B_20260713.json: the play is STOOD DOWN on all four with firehose_present.l1_book FALSE in every case, and B on 0622 recorded that the only book it could see was a Friday object which it carried at explicitly zero weight. Those are traceable STAND-DOWNS, not instances of the mechanism, so they are named here and NOT counted.
audits.condition_can_change_state: CANNOT BE CHECKED, and that is the finding. The bar (|imb10| >= ~0.05) sits on a quantity that is served in no modern decision state and committed in no evidence file. The play's own figure implies 7 of 14 Mondays cleared it, which would make it comfortably live - but that number is not auditable from anything in the repo, and firehose_present.l1_book is false on every modern Monday so it cannot even be evaluated forward.
audits.falsifier: The play carries NO falsifier field, but two are named implicitly in its own text and both are writable: (a) a run of qualifying Mondays where the 06-10 window leans WITH the heavy L1-10 side; (b) a Tue-Thu control run showing the same rate, which would kill the Monday-specificity the play admits is unproven. WHAT WOULD SETTLE THIS PLAY: serve imb10 in decision_state at the Monday 06:00 ET snapshot, or archive the L1-10 book for the seven named derivation Mondays, then re-run. Until one of those exists neither falsifier can be run and the headline cannot be checked by anyone.

audits.the_argument: On a mid-week turn day the prior session's last_hour_dir gates MAGNITUDE: an opposing prior exit means the reversal realizes post-open, so size the confirmed base and never front-run the reactive tail; an aligned exit means momentum carries, so do not cap. The headline support is 'n: 6 opposing-exit reversal days (all D-1 lhd<=0) across g9, g10, g12, g15 = a strikingly consistent signature: EVERY clean mid-week reversal-up day in the record had a prior session that exited DOWN.' That is a base-rate artifact and it is the most important finding in this batch after flow_nowcast. The mechanism was inferred from which days delivered, and the word 'clean' does the selecting.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: Barely. last_hour_dir is -1 on 25 of 40 modern sessions, and over consecutive within-group pairs the prior exited down on 22 of 36 = 61 percent. A claim of the form 'every reversal-up day had a prior exiting down' on n=6 is close to what six random draws give you. And the structure forecloses disconfirmation: the aligned counter-case (g9 0223) is quoted as its own separate arm, so no observation in the record can fall outside one of the two arms.

instances.what_the_state_said: the base rate of the gate's own arming condition: last_hour_dir is -1 on 25 sessions, +1 on 12, 0 on 3; over consecutive same-group pairs the prior exited down 22 of 36
instances.what_the_day_did: the arming condition is TRUE by default 61-63 percent of the time. Any signature keyed on 'the prior exited down' inherits that rate for free

instances.what_the_day_did: 7 of 10 reversal-up days had prior last_hour_dir < 0, against a 61 percent base rate. A lift of about 9 points on n=10 - nothing. THREE reversal-up days had an ALIGNED prior exit: 0527 (prior lhd +1, delivered +620), 0630 (prior lhd +1, +790) and 0717 (prior lhd +1, +190)

instances.what_the_day_did: delivered +760, +70, +530, +790, +230, +200. Median about 530. NOT ONE lands inside the stated band; every one is below its floor. The magnitude band is a winter/spring artefact and does not transfer to the summer regime

instances.what_the_day_did: STOOD DOWN 5 of 5. The gate is refine-only in practice despite being written as an open-time sizing rule, so it has never once sized a blind number

audits.condition_can_change_state: TECHNICALLY YES, PRACTICALLY NO. last_hour_dir takes -1 on 25 / +1 on 12 / 0 on 3 of 40 modern sessions, so the field itself is live and two-sided. But the arming state (prior exited AGAINST the turn) is TRUE 61 percent of the time by default, which is close enough to a constant that a 7-of-10 hit rate is indistinguishable from the base rate - the discrimination disease, not the transfer disease. And the quantity is price-derived, so on a blind day the condition cannot be evaluated at all.
audits.falsifier: The play carries NO falsifier field and its forward_evidence says NONE. The obvious one is already discharged against it on the modern corpus: reversal-up days with an ALIGNED prior exit exist (0527, 0630, 0717) and the opposing-exit magnitude band (+1200..+1600) is missed low by every single modern instance. A real falsifier must be stated as a LIFT over the measured base rate, not as 'every day in the record had X'.

audits.the_argument: Adds two discriminators to the crest-trim trigger, which had fired BOTH ways: (1) based-vs-stretched - crest-trim fires only on a STRETCHED chain near a cum-extreme, never a based one; (2) covering-vs-squaring - price UP into settle AGAINST sell flow is COVERING (forced, positioning_spent, do not fade) rather than genuine same-side squaring at a stretched extreme (the trim). I re-read this under the corrected rubric and it is NOT ASSERTED, which is where S111 put it. The covering-vs-squaring arm is a genuine mechanism - forced covering and voluntary squaring are different acts with different flow signatures - and it has a NAMED FIRST INSTANCE traced to an INDEPENDENT measurement channel, not to the outcome. That is NOVEL_N1 by the rubric's own discriminator, and n=1 is not a reason to downgrade it.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: For the covering arm, yes, and this is the load-bearing point. The classification of 20260327 as covering rests on session and phase signed flow from the MBO evidence store, not on the day's sign: the session closed +1160 UP on total_sflow -2,470 with absorb_session true, and the FINAL phase was the most one-sided sell of the day (-1,878 on 55,181 lots) while price still rose +280. Had 0327 closed up on BUY flow, the tell would have said squaring and the discriminator would have been wrong on its own founding day. For the based-vs-stretched arm, no: it carries no numeric bar on any served quantity, so nothing in the corpus can contradict it, and 0710 shows two readers could class the same day either way. One arm is measured, one is unfalsifiable, and I am classing the play on the arm that is measured.

The covering signature is measured on an independent channel, not inferred from the up close

But NO g14 MBO evidence file exists in the repo, so unlike 0327 the squaring flow tell here is NOT independently traceable - which is exactly what the play itself admits when it says the flow tell is 'MBO-proven G15, inferred otherwise'

audits.the_argument: The covering-absorption UP tell is not unconditional - its SIGN flips with extension. Young / low-extension absorption of a dip is short-covering UP; maximally extended (cum above about +2000 from the block anchor AND chain age >= 5) with the absorption tell ITSELF reversed is late chasers being absorbed, which is DISTRIBUTION DOWN. The support is 'g19: UP on 0515, DOWN on 0520; the pair is the discriminator; 0519 was AT extension but absorption had not reversed, so correctly NOT flipped'. Three days, one block, and all three readings were produced by the REFINE with the realized price curve in hand. The mechanism - late chasers absorbed equals distribution - was inferred from which way the days went, not tested against anything independent. The play states its own weakness plainly and to its credit: 'n=3 within one block, needs a second block'.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: Marginally, within the block: 0519 is a real non-fire at extension and it could have flipped and did not. But the discriminator has three free terms (a cum bar, an age bar, and absorption-reversal) fitted to three days by a refine that knew all three answers. One term per observation is a guaranteed fit. The one component that IS a real measured correction is the assumption_retired block, and it is the best-supported thing in the entry.

audits.the_argument: A deterministic SCHEDULE rather than a signal: a play keyed on cum_from_anchor or chain extension may assert a RUNG only for k <= 3 sessions from the block anchor; from k >= 4 it widens to the full band or stands down. It rests on a single aggregate measurement - mean |constructed cum - realized cum| by k across G17-G20 - plus the structural observation that k is known in advance in a one-shot block blind, so nothing has to be inferred at runtime. It is one of only two plays in this batch whose evidence is a re-runnable aggregate over committed files rather than a narrative of days, and it is the only one that also carries a written forward test with an explicit kill condition.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: Yes, decisively, and in two separate ways. A flat divergence profile would have killed it outright. A smooth accumulation would have made the k<=3 boundary arbitrary - independent random-walk accumulation of uncorrelated daily errors predicts only about 1.15x growth at the k=3 to k=4 step, against the 2.13x measured in the derivation set and 1.91x forward. Neither null happened, so the kink is real and is evidence of CORRELATED (block-lean) error rather than mechanical accumulation - which is the play's implicit mechanism and it survives its own null.

The support is a full-corpus aggregate over committed files with per-event listing, a stated base-rate comparison, a DECLARED NEGATIVE CONTROL, a written falsifier, and an honest D24 declaration in its forward field ('CORPUS SEARCHED, INSTANCES FOUND ... all 70 sessions'). Alongside chain_staleness_gate it is one of only two plays in this batch whose evidence is a re-runnable aggregate rather than a narrative of days.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: Yes, at four thresholds independently and on both sides of the tape - and it DID come out otherwise on the one arm that decides usability. The D-1 arm is a null (4/9, 6/11) and the play REPORTS the null rather than burying it, then converts the play into a PROHIBITION on the strength of it. That is the opposite of the S108 signature. The one part that is genuinely unsupported is the causal STORY for the asymmetry (persistent offer-side supply from producer hedging, index roll, call overwriting) - that is a plausible reading of the numbers, nothing in the corpus separates it from other explanations, and it is not what the play's instruction depends on.

audits.the_argument: Claim: when aggressor flow is flat, fade the heavy resting side - an ask-heavy book means price runs UP through it, 'wall = fuel, not floor'. The entire support is one cross-sectional split in legacy_notes.evidence: ask-heavy legs go up 0.61 (n=158), bid-heavy 0.42 (n=121). That number is a real measurement and it is NOT the outcome the play was written to explain, so this is not OUTCOME_CREDITED. It is also not ASSERTED - there is a number and there is a stated mechanism. But it is a single POOLED read over 279 legs from the 12 warm-season days of S92, in direct violation of this desk's standing 'per-cell always, never pool' rule, with no per-cell breakdown, no null, no monotone-in-strength check (which the sibling direction.flow_nowcast does carry), and no replication. The play's own forward field reads 'NONE. Derived on the warm-season set; never re-tested on any later block. Zero forward evidence.' And the same evidence block records 'flow_beats_book_when_disagree 262/293 = 0.89', which scopes the play to the residual 11% of disagreement cases. I cannot classify it higher without a per-cell re-run and I cannot classify it lower without discarding a real measurement, so it is UNCLEAR and I say below exactly what would settle it.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: YES for the original split - 0.61/0.42 could have come back 0.50/0.50 and did not. NO for anything since: in the entire g17-g23 corpus the play has never been evaluated on a single day, so no test capable of refuting it has been run in five years of walk. The causal story ('wall = fuel') is layered on top of the correlation and was never tested against the obvious alternative (the heavy resting side is where informed capital sits and price is drawn toward it). This project's own OD history is the reason to be careful with exactly this evidence shape: CLAUDE.md records that apparent directional lifts from pooled flow reads 'were trend/base-rate artifacts (Simpson's on a trending window) and died under window/forward sweep + temporal OOS'.

audits.the_argument: Two separable arms. (i) SIZE: up-size the storage-Thursday magnitude prior. (ii) SIDE: the post-print LEG sides with the running chain, never the print sign, and the DAY NET is owned by the chain state. The SIZE arm is measurable and I measured it (below). The SIDE arm is the problem and it is the reason for the class. Its evidence field is a 10,000-character per-event narrative whose every entry has the form 'date, realized net, the chain was X, so the chain won' - the chain label is read at the same moment as the outcome, and the rule is confirmed by the outcome. Not one count in that block could have gone the other way. More telling: every counterexample produced a NEW conditioning dimension rather than a refutation. 1120 became the leg-vs-net split (S97.2); the G9 bullish-draw sells became polarity (S98.2); 0129/0205/0212 became spent-chain scoping (S101.3); the G14 blind became chain-state-is-tape-state (S102.1); 0326 became an entirely new play (magnitude.shoulder_counter_print_damping). Five successive rescues, each on n<=3. The forward field's headline '14 storage Thursdays, every one leg-sided with the running chain' is a 14/14 record for a rule the same file documents breaking at 1120, 0129 and 0326 - the 14/14 survives only because each break was first reclassified into a different arm.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: SIZE arm: YES, and I ran it - it could have come back at parity and it did not (1.65x pooled), and it DOES come back badly per-block in the two summer blocks. SIDE arm: NO. 'The chain won' is unfalsifiable once the chain can be relabelled live / spent / young / basing after the fact, and the play's own history is a record of exactly that relabelling. The leg-side arm is also not independently re-measurable from the committed corpus: g<N>_mbo_evidence.json serves three coarse phases per day (sflow / pxchg / vol), not a print-anchored decomposition, so nobody can recompute 'leg-sided with the chain' from the record even if they wanted to.

audits.the_argument: Claim: a chain polarity flip needs an ARM (parabolic run >=~1.5-2x the prior largest swing, >=~9 sessions, plus a >=30%-off blow-off close) and a four-condition CONFIRM (C1 band-break >=1.5x, C2 old-side continuation-collapse, C3 printed-never-front-run, C4 catalyst arbiter). This is the best-supported play in the batch and the support is falsification-shaped, not narrative. The per-instance table carries counts that could have gone the other way: C1 fires 1008 / 1020 / 1208 / 1223 / 0120 / 0302 and correctly DECLINES 0107 - six fires, one correct decline, zero false positives across G4/G5/G9/G10/G11/G14. It carries a documented FALSE POSITIVE (G10 0108) and a documented FALSE NEGATIVE (G11 0120) on opposite sides of the same bar, and says so in its own text. C2's ratio reformulation was REFUTED on comparable data (0120 true 0.714 vs 0107 false 0.718, near-identical on every arm) and was KEPT-AND-SCOPED rather than quietly dropped. C2's absolute arm is explicitly declared non-discriminating above ~160 legs / 75k trades. A negative control is named (G7 1113: blow-off form fired, swing only 0.55x the prior, correctly no flip). The problem is not the support. It is that the play has been dormant for nine blocks and its requires field is wrong about the architecture it now runs in.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: YES, repeatedly and demonstrably - this is the one play in my batch whose evidence has visibly been allowed to embarrass it. 0107 could have fired C1 and did not. 0120 could have fired C2 and did not, and the play recorded that as its own false negative rather than reclassifying it. The scale-invariant ratio reformulation was built expecting it would separate true from false, returned 0.714 vs 0.718, and the refutation was written into the play. The G11 block reversed +17,140 against a declined flip and the play absorbed that as a false negative and cut its own confidence 0.5 -> 0.4.

TWO THINGS WOULD SETTLE IT, both cheap: serve the prior day's realized net (or the condition-class band table) in the blind state, and re-derive the bands for the modern amplitude regime, where the historical 1,800-5,010 fires sit at or above the corpus maximum day move of 2,100.

audits.the_argument: Claim: a failed counter-flush in the final 30-75 min, IN CONJUNCTION with a live structural pull state (delivery week / squeeze_watch / crowded short base), precedes squeeze ignition - 3/3 on 0130, 1223, 0129 spanning G9/G11; the flush alone is named NOISE. The retrospective around it is unusually disciplined and I want that on the record: it demotes F6 (trade-rate ramp) and F7 (VWAP posture) to NOISE because they fire on quiet-day controls, demotes F3/F4/F5 to WATCH for failing the spanning requirement, names 1128 as a 'WEAK-TELL INSTANCE, named honestly', names 1020's missing raw tape as a limit, and records G13 as a clean negative block. That is better conduct than most of the corpus. But the play underneath has the outcome-credited shape: the three instances were SELECTED as days that ignited, the pre-onset signature was found looking backwards, and when the one control that challenged it showed the flush-fail ALSO fires on quiet days (0219, 0212), the response was to ADD the conjunction limb rather than retract. The conjunction limb has never itself been varied - all three instances carry it, and no instance exists anywhere where the conjunction fired and ignition did not follow.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: PARTLY, and the part that could is real. The quiet-day controls could have shown the flush-fail was clean and they did not; that measurement was allowed to come out badly and it killed F6, F7 and the compression read. But the SURVIVING rule has no test capable of refuting it: a squeeze-regime day carrying a failed flush that did NOT ignite has never been looked for, and the controls used were quiet days which by construction lack the conjunction's second limb. The version that was falsified is not the version that was kept.

audits.the_argument: Claim: in an S1-VOID shoulder (near-window normals base <=~20 gw-HDD), a print whose fundamental would trade AGAINST the running chain has its DAY NET damped toward flat, because S1-void removes the seasonal amplifier that turns a fundamental into a big directional day. The evidence field says n=1 and names the event: 0326, 'Blind sized +900 on the 0129 spent-chain-with-print form; actual +480 midday round-tripped to -60.' The exemplar IS the miss the play was written to explain, and the mechanism was chosen after the round-trip rather than tested against it. Two things are to its credit and I weighed them: it carries a real CONTROL (rejected_alternative: 0319, chain-sided in the same S1-void, delivered -1,080, which kills the broader 'damp all shoulder prints' version and forces the scoping to counter prints only), and its G16 forward note is honest that the counter arm was NOT exercised because G16 contained no counter print. So the standing is one instance, one control on a WIDER claim, and zero forward exercises of its own arm in ten sessions of merge history. It is not NOVEL_N1 because the instance is not a first sighting of something new - it is the reinterpretation of a miss.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: NO for the play's own arm. One day round-tripped and a mechanism was selected to explain the round-trip. The 0319 control could have come out otherwise and did real work, but it constrains a different, broader claim. The winter_contrast (0129/0205/0212 delivering +1,480/+540/+120) is the same three days already used to build the spent-chain rule inside daytype.storage_thursday_magnitude, so it is not an independent measurement here - it is the same evidence counted twice in two plays.

audits.the_argument: Claim: when a DOWN-chain is mature (age>=3), price sits at a cum-extreme or origin shelf, and the prior 1-2 sessions carry an exhaustion tell (large sell flow ABSORBED with price holding, or an extreme big-print sell-climax closing at the low), the next mid-week day is a give-back-exhaustion reversal UP, not the chain-resume DOWN the blind keeps calling. Every one of the seven evidence entries has the identical form 'blind X, ACTUAL Y': g15 0318 blind -400 / actual +1,900; g15 0325 blind +250 / actual +660; g12 0203/0204 blind -750/-850 / actual +1,130/+1,260; g10 0107 blind -550 / actual +1,500; g9 0217 blind -800 / actual +1,890; g14 0303 blind -650 / actual +640. The instance set IS the blind's biggest mid-week misses and the rule is a description of what they had in common. The play is admirably explicit about its own nature - 'It is a SELECTOR/recognition failure, not a missing rule' - which is honest but does not change the support class. forward_evidence: NONE, self-declared. There is one negative control (g15 0324, young chain, correctly continued down) and two out-of-scope exclusions (g13 0217, g16 0401). No base rate for the configuration was ever measured before the rule was written from seven of its positive outcomes.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: NO as assembled. Days were selected because they reversed; the tell was then read backwards off those days. The single negative control fails the AGE limb, not the EXHAUSTION limb - so the load-bearing limb has never been tested against a day that carried it and continued down. My corpus scan below could have found the configuration recurring and delivering, and instead found it occurs twice in 60 served days and delivers one sixth of the stated magnitude on the only clean instance.

audits.the_argument: Claim: burn confirms that weather-driven demand ARRIVED; it does not price it, because burn is a numerator with no balance-clearing denominator. Therefore burn may confirm, may DAMP a lean that contradicts it, but may NEVER license a directional lean of its own and must never act as a SUPPRESSOR before magnitude is derived. This is a PROHIBITION, and it was born out of the hardest event in the corpus: the retirement of its own predecessor, weather.burn_conversion_gate, on that gate's named forward test, by four specialists including its author. The mechanism is causal and checkable (a rate with no stock term cannot say whether the arriving demand clears the surplus), and it was tested with numbers that came out badly and were published anyway - D-0716 reports the balance term as 2/3 as a gate revocation and 4/7 as a standalone direction sorter and explicitly declines to claim it as one; E offers its own reformulation as 'a MEASUREMENT TO RUN, not a play to fire (n=1 clean)'; the forward field opens with the words 'HONEST AND THIN'. That is the conduct this audit exists to reward.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: YES, decisively, and it did - this play exists BECAUSE the previous version's written falsifier discharged against it. The predecessor's falsifier was 'a burn-confirmed CDD add that fails to deliver, in G23+'; C-0708 found three clean up-fires in G23 delivering 0 of 3, and D-0709 found the CDD-add limb was a CONSTANT (positive 20/20 days across two groups) - a limb that never changes sign cannot gate. The successor's own numbers (2/3, 4/7) were then reported unflatteringly rather than rounded up.

audits.the_argument: A conditional continuation rate that rises with the favourable peak already reached: $50->0.43, $150->0.57, $250->0.75, $350->0.92, $500->1.00, derived on 372 legs over 12 warm-season days (S92), n=38 at the $350 rung and n=11 at $500. 'continuation' is defined in month_characterize.move_path as retention >= 0.5 where retention = end-of-1800s-window favourable excursion divided by peak. That is a real rate on a real conditioning variable and it is the one play in this batch that can be re-run, because renders/ng_refine_s95/fingerprints.json stores peak_usd, retention, continuation, time_to_peak_s and peaked_fast for 6,358 legs across 108 days - 98 of which post-date the derivation window. I re-ran it. THE SHAPE SURVIVES PERFECTLY AND THE LEVELS DO NOT: 0.386 / 0.519 / 0.626 / 0.713 / 0.823 against the claimed 0.43 / 0.57 / 0.75 / 0.92 / 1.00, monotone at every rung, with the shortfall widening as size rises (-0.04 at $50, -0.21 at $350, -0.18 at $500). The headline the runbook carries - 'the $350 crossing = a 92% keep-riding event; $500 = 100%' - is a small-n artifact; at n=1,307 and n=638 the true rates are 71% and 82%. Per cell, never pooled, the $350 rung holds at 0.701 hard_heat / 0.758 mod_heat / 0.652 unknown / 0.723 up-legs / 0.702 down-legs, so it is a stable relationship, not a regime accident. THE CAUSAL READING IS THE PART THAT DOES NOT HOLD: within a fixed 1800s window, median time-to-peak climbs monotonically with the peak bucket (12s / 454s / 924s / 1,146s / 1,343s / 1,521s), and since retention is end-over-peak, a leg that peaks at 1,521 of 1,800 seconds has only 279 seconds left in which to give back. Holding size fixed, timing dominates: in the 150-350 bucket peaked_fast legs continue 2 of 32 (0.063) against 729 of 1,863 (0.391) for slow peaks, a six-fold spread; in the 50-150 bucket, 6 of 226 (0.027) against 231 of 1,491 (0.155). So the staircase is largely SIZE ACTING AS A PROXY FOR TIME-TO-PEAK, which is what shape.grind_vs_spike already says causally ('grind holds, front-loaded spike round-trips'). The play also declares its own tension and I want that on the record as honesty rather than as a defect: status STABLE, confidence 0.90, forward_evidence 'NONE beyond derivation... Its high confidence reflects derivation strength, not forward evidence.'
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: Yes, emphatically, and I made it try. A mean-reverting tape would have produced a flat or descending staircase; it did not, at 6,358 legs, on 98 days outside the derivation window, and per cell. The rung LEVELS did come out otherwise - every one of them, in the same direction - which is exactly what a falsifiable measurement is supposed to be able to do. What could NOT have come out otherwise is the causal attribution to size: nothing in the derivation separates size from time-to-peak, and when I separate them the timing variable carries most of the effect.

audits.the_argument: The entire support is a list of five days on which the blind's guess was smaller than the realized move, with the conclusion 'on catalyst days the actual dominant move DWARFED the guess'. I traced all five to forecasts/grp5.json and every number is exact: 1008 guess +320 / actual -1,980; 1010 +150 / -1,490; 1016 -300 / -1,190; 1020 +580 / +2,770; 1021 +440 / +1,100. So the evidence is real and honestly recorded. But it is a RESIDUAL LOG, not a test - the evidence field is the forecast error, and the claim is that the forecast error exists. AND THE LOG DOES NOT MEASURE WHAT THE PLAY CLAIMS: two of the five exemplars are WRONG-SIGN days, not undersized days. On 1008 the guess was +320 and the actual was -1,980; on 1010 the guess was +150 and the actual was -1,490. A day whose sign was wrong carries no information about whether the magnitude scale is too small, and folding two sign misses into a five-item scale claim inflates it by 40%. Only 1016 (4x under), 1020 (4.8x under) and 1021 (2.5x under) are right-signed under-calls and can bear the argument. To the play's credit it refuses to act on itself - status HYPOTHESIS, confidence 0.30, call 'CANDIDATE correction ONLY... Do NOT globally rescale', an explicit ANTI-LOCK-IN clause holding a rival reading (higher-vol autumn regime) open, and forward_evidence 'SUPERSEDED... Winter bands replaced it from G7 onward.' I considered NOT_A_PLAY on those grounds and rejected it: it has a trigger, a read and a call, it makes a substantive magnitude claim, and classifying it out would lose the finding about its evidence.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: No. Every item is a realized forecast error on a day chosen because the error was large. There is no denominator - the days on which the warm-season guess was the right size, or too big, were never counted - and no control regime. The one part that COULD have come out otherwise is the sign audit I ran on the play's own list, and it came out against the play: 2 of 5 exemplars are sign misses masquerading as scale misses.

audits.the_argument: A set of per-event magnitude bands for the winter post-flip regime, and each band is literally the realized nets of the days that produced it with a line drawn around them: 'flip-confirm + chained crash -2400..-2900 (1208 -2730, 1209 -2840)', 'print-liquidity crash -1800..-4000 (1211 -3970, 1218 -1830, 1224 -2450)', and so on for six classes. The class LABELS were assigned to the days after the outcome split them. THE FORWARD CLAIM IS CIRCULAR AND THE CIRCLE IS VISIBLE INSIDE THE PLAY: forward_evidence reads 'FORWARD-CONFIRMED on G10 (both January crashes landed in band)', and the two January crashes are 0109 -2,760 and 0114 -2,710 - which the call field then writes in as the S99.2 bleed band's own defining exemplars ('crash -2400..-2900 SINGLE-day (0109 -2760, 0114 -2710)'). A genuine forward test was performed and then absorbed into the fit, so those two days can never test the bands again. AND A WHOLE GROUP'S FORWARD RECORD IS MISSING. The play fired SIX times in G12 - forecasts/grp12.json plays_fired on 0206, 0209, 0210, 0211, 0212, 0213 - and neither the forward field nor the g11_note mentions G12 at all. Scored against g12_score.json: -1,100 vs -1,160; -1,100 vs -830; +450 vs +240; -950 vs +610; -750 vs +110; -300 vs -1,400. Direction 4 of 6, and the block's largest down day was called at 4.7x too small. Worse, none of those six days is inside the play's own stated trigger ('sizing day-nets after a confirmed polarity flip'): the largest G12 move was -1,400, nowhere near the crash classes. The play was being used as a general magnitude lookup outside its regime, six times, unrecorded. Finally the G11 note contains an escape that makes the play unfalsifiable on its only claim: '0130 +5020 (guessed +300... ~17x)' is dismissed with 'the fires were band-selection calls made under a wrong polarity, which is the polarity input's issue, not the bands'.' If a 17x magnitude miss is never the magnitude play's fault, nothing can ever be.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: The band derivation, no - the numbers in each band ARE the outcomes the band was drawn around, and the condition classes were assigned after the split. The G10 forward check, yes, genuinely - a band derived in December either contains two January days or it does not, and it did; but re-listing those same two days as the bleed band's exemplars spent that test. The G12 record, yes, and it was never assembled: 4 of 6 on direction with one 4.7x magnitude miss is a real result that nobody banked.

audits.the_argument: A post-onset confirm rather than a predictor: in a THIN regime only, price progressing hard through sell-dominant prints (progress per 1,000 lots at roughly 2x the day baseline, 38-47 ticks per thousand on 0121 and 1223 against controls at or below 17) is read as offers being WITHDRAWN rather than buyers attacking - the F2 fingerprint from the S101 squeeze retrospective. The mechanism is a real microstructure distinction (supply removal versus demand arrival produce the same price path but opposite lot-efficiency), the two instances are named, a quantitative separation is stated with named controls, and a NEGATIVE result is declared rather than hidden: 'Non-discriminating on liquid tapes (1128) - thin regimes only.' Confidence 0.5, status PROVISIONAL, forward_evidence 'NONE'. That combination - argued mechanism, named instances, declared scope limit, honest zero forward evidence - is NOVEL_N1 as the rubric defines it, and n=2 with a control is if anything stronger than the class requires. I am NOT upgrading it to MECHANISM_VERIFIED, because I could not verify a single number in it. The discriminating quantity, progress per 1,000 lots, is not computed in any committed file: renders/ng_refine_s95/fingerprints.json carries peak_usd, retention and the turn markers but no volume or lot field; g*_mbo_evidence.json carries phase sflow and pxchg but no lot-normalised progress; and price is masked in the blind state by design. The two exemplar DAYS are traceable - 20260121 net_actual +3,820 in g11_score.json, 20251223 actual +5,010 in g9_score.json - but the ratchet reading on them is not stored anywhere I can open. Every one of the fifteen corpus appearances is a stand-down, and in each case for the same declared reason: squeeze_watch's spread limb is genuinely price-masked so calendar_limb_satisfied_live is null, or calendar_dte_limb_satisfied_live is false at dte 16-21 against a <=7 window. The specialists stood it down as UNKNOWN rather than as negative, which is the correct handling and is worth recording as a positive about the run discipline.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: As described, yes - the play states a numeric separation (38-47 versus <=17 ticks per thousand lots) with named controls on both sides, and 1128 is a declared non-separating liquid tape, which is a negative result that could have killed the scoping. But I cannot confirm that any of it was computed the way it is described, because the quantity does not exist in the committed corpus. So the honest answer is: the SHAPE of the evidence is falsifiable; its CONTENT is unverifiable from here.
audits.condition_can_change_state: UNKNOWABLE from the committed corpus, and that is the finding. The trigger has two limbs: a thin-regime gate and progress-per-1,000-lots >= ~2x the day baseline. The lot-normalised progress is not stored in fingerprints.json, in any g*_mbo_evidence.json, or in any grp*_state.json, so the bar cannot be evaluated on a single day of the walk. What I CAN say is that the play's gating sibling is degenerate in the modern blocks: squeeze_watch.calendar_dte_limb_satisfied_live is false across G22 at dte 18-21 and the spread limb is masked all block, which is why all fifteen corpus appearances are stand-downs.
audits.falsifier: The brain's falsifier field is EMPTY. The play's own scope note supplies half of one ('non-discriminating on liquid tapes'), which means a thin-regime session showing the ratchet fingerprint and then failing to sustain would discharge it. WHAT WOULD SETTLE THE WHOLE THING: a leg-grain replay that computes ticks-per-1,000-lots per session and writes it into the evidence store alongside phase sflow, then re-scores 20260121 and 20251223 against a matched set of thin non-squeeze sessions. Until that field is served, this play is unexercisable and unauditable, and it should not accumulate confidence in either direction.

audits.the_argument: THIS IS THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL FINDING IN MY BATCH, because the play is a SELECTOR - the machinery that decides which angle wins a bimodal split - and its up-arm has never been reachable. The rule defaults a storage-versus-weather split to the S3-bearish DOWN angle, and lets the weather-cold-add UP angle win ONLY IF BOTH gates hold: (a) near-window D0..D+3 max forecast gw-HDD >= ~16.4, AND (b) session_b_share >= ~0.50. I evaluated both gates day by day on every staged group that serves them. GATE (a) FIRES 0 OF 10 IN G18, 0 OF 10 IN G19, 0 OF 10 IN G20, 0 OF 10 IN G21, 0 OF 10 IN G22 AND 0 OF 10 IN G23 - zero of sixty, with block maxima of 11.46, 6.06, 2.95, 0.80, 0.37 and 0.24 against a 16.4 bar. In the winter blocks it is degenerate the other way, 12 of 12 in G12 and 12 of 12 in G13. It splits days only in the shoulder, 8 of 12 in G14 and 7 of 12 in G15. In the BIRTH BLOCK G16 it fires on exactly ONE day out of eleven - 0405, at 16.93 - and that one day is the play's own named positive control. GATE (b) fires 3 of 88 served sessions (3.4%), which is the S108 normalization defect the brain already records. THE CONJUNCTION - the up-angle unlock, the entire discriminating content of the selector - IS SATISFIED ON 0 OF THE 82 DAY-ROWS across nine staged groups where both gates are evaluable. It has never once been possible for the weather angle to win. The evidence field is 'n: 3 splits IN this block, all resolved DOWN correctly by the gates' - and I verified all three against g16_score.json (0401 -600, 0406 -470, 0407 -220, exact). But G16 closed DOWN on 10 of 11 days (-790, -650, -110, -600, -130, +400, -470, -220, -450, -610, -190). A gate that can only ever emit DOWN, scored on a block that was down 91% of the time, gets 3 of 3 by construction. The brain's own negative_result_reported blames gate (b) and names the G20 symptom (sub-0.50 on 10 of 10 in a block that rallied +1,860) without identifying that gate (a) is worse and unconditional. AND THE CORPUS ALREADY KNEW: grp21_mbo_specialist_C wrote 'selector.divergence_resolution arm (a)... cannot fire in June by construction - the same failure shape as the b_share bar that was just fixed, on the other axis.' That was scoped to one block and never reached the brain.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: NO, and this is the strongest form of the failure. The play's three supporting instances all resolve DOWN because DOWN is the only output the gates can produce; the 'positive control' 0405 clears gate (a) but fails gate (b), so it is not a control on the rule as written either. There is no configuration of the served data, on any of 82 evaluable day-rows across nine groups, in which the evidence could have come out UP. An arm that cannot fire cannot be wrong, and cannot be right.

audits.the_argument: The claim is that a fresh chain (age 0-1), chain-sided, with aligned D-1 flow delivers the FULL class band and must not get the counter-print damping - and the derived magnitude is stated as 'full class band (young chain-sided ran +1950..+5010 vs capped blinds +120..+800)'. That range IS the three realized moves, and the capped range IS the three blind guesses. The evidence is three days on which the blind under-forecast badly, with the class label attached afterwards. I traced all three and every number verifies - but TWO OF THE THREE DATES ARE MIS-WRITTEN IN THE BRAIN, with the leading digit dropped. 'g9 0223 Tue young_turn_chain_extension: blind +600, ACTUAL +5010' is 20251223 (g9_score.json: guess +600, actual +5,010, archetype 'young_turn_chain_extension', dow Tue - exact). 'g8 0119 Wed post_stabilization_hold_drift_up: blind +120, ACTUAL +1950' is 20251119 (g8_score.json: guess +120, actual +1,950, archetype 'post_stabilization_hold_drift_up', dow Wed - exact). As written, 0223 falls inside G13's window and 0119 inside G11's, so anyone re-tracing goes to the wrong block and finds nothing. The third, 'g14 0311', is correct (g14_score.json: guess +800, actual +2,030). THE MISSING PIECE IS THE DENOMINATOR. Three days delivered a full band. How many days met the same trigger - chain age 0-1, chain-sided, D-1 flow aligned - and did NOT deliver one was never counted, and cannot be counted from the committed corpus, because chain age and chain-sided classification are derived narrative labels, not served fields. So the play's rate is 3 of 3 out of an unknown population, and the class labels in the score files were themselves assigned in the same post-mortem that produced the play. I also note the play carries NO confidence field at all and its falsifier field is empty, while its does_not_explain clause is the only real constraint on it.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: No. All three instances are days selected because the actual dwarfed the blind; the band is the set of those actuals; the class name was assigned after the fact by the same pass. There is no negative instance anywhere in the record - no young chain-sided aligned-flow day that failed to extend - and no counted population from which 3 of 3 could be a rate rather than a list.

audits.the_argument: A SIGN play: recurring big-print buy-absorption (big_print_b_share >= 0.55 on >= 2 of the last ~5 sessions, NON-consecutive) under a sub-0.50 sell tape against an extreme-and-worsening COT short is ACCUMULATION rather than down-continuation, so move the sign toward the turn. THE DISCRIMINATING PARAMETER WAS FITTED TO THE OUTCOME, AND THE PLAY SAYS SO IN ITS OWN CONFIDENCE FIELD: 'the window fix (~5 non-consecutive) is what makes the arm catch spaced accumulation; the strict 2-of-3 missed G17 entirely.' The window was widened from 2-of-3 to >=2-of-~5 after the fact, and the acceptance test for the widening was that the arm then fired on 0422 - the day the G17 block turned. grp17_mbo_specialist_C states the loop explicitly: 'A strict 2-of-3-consecutive window sees zero of this and rides the S3-down default straight through the turn - which is exactly the blind's 0415/0422 misses.' A free parameter tuned until the rule fires on a known outcome is the definition of the class. THE CREDIT IS ALSO A REFINE NUMBER, not a blind one: grp17_mbo_refined_r2.json records 0422 refined +130 against actual +140 with weight_assigned blind 0.30 / causal_mbo 0.70, so 70% of the number came from a read that had the price curve. AND THE ARM'S OWN NEXT TEST FAILED - the forward field records 'C's 0506 RTS-up was wrong (buy-absorb-failing DOWN)'; g18 0506 closed -530. I ran the literal arm over every core Tue/Wed day in g18-g23 on the served state. It fires three times: 20260603 (+750 UP, correct), 20260616 (+970 UP, correct), 20260617 (-970 DOWN, wrong). But on the basis the brain has NOW LICENSED - the sub-0.50 limb must read session_b_share_two_sided - 0616 dissolves (two-sided 0.520 fails the sub-0.50 limb) and G20 is unevaluable (two-sided is served only from G21). audits.the_argument: A weekend or holiday reopen seam in a crowded-short regime carries a DIRECTIONAL gap prior: a WORSENING COT WoW means the seam is the covering rally's firing window, so attach an UP gap prior; a FLAT WoW means no prior and the gap reverts to noise. The mechanism is a loaded-spring argument and the birth evidence is better than it looks: g19's two weekends fired an IDENTICAL +580 up gap from OPPOSITE inherited exit states (0511 an aligned-sell press, 0518 a covering close-on-high), which is a real control - if the gap were carried by the inherited state the two would have differed. That is a measurement that could have come out otherwise. WHAT NOBODY EVER DID WAS ASSEMBLE THE SEAM TALLY, so I did. Armed means MM 1y percentile below ~3 and chg_wow negative, read off the served COT at each seam. ARMED SEAMS: 20260511 +580, 20260518 +580, 20260601 +690, 20260615 -750, 20260622 +1,210 - FOUR OF FIVE UP, mean +462. UNARMED SEAMS: 20260427 -50, 20260504 +440, 20260525 -240, 20260629 +50, 20260706 -580, 20260713 -360 - two of six up, mean -123. THE INSTANCE THE BRAIN NEVER RECORDED IS 20260622, AND IT IS THE MOST INTERESTING DAY IN MY BATCH. It is armed by the IDENTICAL COT reading that armed the 0615 falsifier - report 2026-06-09, MM net -122,617, pctile 2.83, chg_wow -7,763 - because the next report did not publish until 2026-06-22 15:30 ET, after the Sunday reopen, and the state correctly serves it at age_days 9.35. Same armed state, one week apart, gapped -750 and then +1,210. Meanwhile grp22_B_20260622 stood the play down and wrote 'The four scorable walk seams run +580/+690/-350/-750 = a coin flip' - a tally that omits g19's second +580 and INCLUDES 20260608 (-350), which is not armed at all (chg_wow +19,572, improving). B then emitted a +20 gap against a realized +1,210. This is S110's structural lesson recurring verbatim: a tally assembled from independent slices is systematically incomplete and must be recomputed at the coordinator.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: Yes, at birth and forward. At birth the two g19 seams had opposite inherited exit states and could have gapped opposite ways; they did not. audits.the_argument: The microstructure mechanism is sound and I want that said first: a large resting order is filled BY the crowd, so a program working the offer prints aggressor-BUY while price falls. That is correct market mechanics and it generalises a case A had already named for covering shorts. The instances are real and traced: G21 0608 printed +3,261 of net aggressor buy while falling -890 with absorb_session TRUE, and G23 0715 printed +6,326 of buy - the block's largest tilt - and closed -60 on BCOM roll day 5, with C matching the ph2 fingerprint to within ten units of 0608 (+2,858/-120 versus +2,868/+40). WHAT IS NOT TESTED IS THE DISCRIMINATION, which is where the play's whole content lives: the claim is not that aggressor tilts invert, it is that they invert ON PROGRAM DAYS, so a same-signed tilt there is SUSPECT. I ran that directly. Joining g*_mbo_evidence.json total_sflow to g*_actual.json day moves gives 59 sessions in g18-g23 with both a nonzero tilt and a nonzero move. On the 21 program-or-expiry days the tilt AGREES with the day sign 12 times (57.1%). On the 38 other days it agrees 13 times (34.2%). So the aggressor tilt inverts 65.8% of the time on ORDINARY days and only 42.9% of the time on program days - the inversion is a general property of this tape and program days are, if anything, the LEAST inverted. Per group, never pooled as the conclusion, the program-day agreement rate is greater than or equal to the non-program rate in five of six blocks (g18 1/3 vs 0/7, g19 3/4 vs 2/6, g20 1/2 vs 3/8, g21 2/5 vs 2/5, g22 1/1 vs 4/8, g23 4/6 vs 2/4). The play named the two program days out of twenty-one that inverted. And its own third instance points the same way: 0714 fired limb one of the play's falsifier (tilt +3,747 buy, day +200 up, on a GSCI-and-BCOM roll day) and was set aside on limb two, 'the program is demonstrably the dominant participant' - a condition no served field measures. C was right not to bank a falsification it could not show; the defect is that the falsifier was written with a limb that can never be evaluated.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: For the mechanism, yes, and it holds - a 65.8% baseline inversion rate is a real, falsifiable property of this tape and it is the play's genuine contribution. For the DISCRIMINATION, no: two program days were selected from twenty-one by their outcome, the control condition was never run, and the falsifier's second limb is unmeasurable. When I run the control it comes out against the play at 57.1% versus 34.2% - which at n=21 versus n=38 is about 1.7 sigma, so not decisive, but it certainly is not support.

audits.the_argument: D-1 rally QUALITY is claimed to sort next-day magnitude: an ALIGNED rally holds, a CONVICTION-NEGATIVE pop (rise on net-sell or absorption) gives back 50-70% next session, and covering-financed up-legs get credit only to the reversal-reclaim. The founding pair is genuinely well designed and it verifies exactly: 20260630 rose +790 with ph2 sflow -4,266 against pxchg +880, ph_absorb TRUE and absorb_session TRUE, and 20260701 gave back -500 = 63%; 20260624 rose the SAME +790 on aligned phases (+296/+84/-69), absorb_session FALSE, and 20260625 held at -60. Same magnitude, opposite conviction, opposite sequel - that is a controlled comparison and it could have come out otherwise. BUT THE BAND IS ONE DAY'S OUTCOME. '50-70%' is the single realized give-back on 0701 (63%) with a range drawn around it, and I tested it. Over every D-1-up-leg to next-session pair within a group in g17-g23 (g*_mbo_evidence.json joined to actuals), conviction-negative days number 21: the next day closes DOWN 12 times (57%), the median give-back is 21%, and ONLY 2 OF 21 land in the prescribed 50-70% band. Aligned days number 12: next day DOWN 6 times (50%), 1 of 12 in band. I ran two further operationalizations in case mine was too loose - strict absorb_session gives 8/14 (57%) versus 10/19 (53%) with 1 and 2 in band; absorb-or-final-phase-absorb gives 12/20 (60%) versus 6/13 (46%) with 1 and 2 in band. So the DIRECTIONAL half has a weak but consistent lean in the claimed direction across all three definitions (57-60% against 46-53%), and the MAGNITUDE half - which is the play's actual call, it is a magnitude play - is not supported anywhere: the prescribed band captures one or two cases in fourteen to twenty-one. ITS FIRST OUT-OF-BLOCK APPLICATION CONTRADICTS IT. In grp23_B_20260706 the play fires, correctly classifies 0703 as a conviction-negative pop (net +410 on sflow -1,005, absorb_session TRUE), prescribes '-200..-290' of give-back and caps the session at +100. The realized session net was +680 UP - the day move was only +100 because the gap was -580, a component this play does not govern. B then invoked the play's own 'no new driver' escape on the same day, so the adverse instance was neutralised at the moment it occurred.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: The 0624-versus-0630 pair, yes - two same-sized up-legs with different conviction could have produced the same sequel and did not, which is real. The BAND, no - 50-70% is one realized give-back with a bracket around it, and there is no population behind it. The forward claim 'n>=3 instances spanning g19/g22' is not a rate either; I could locate the g22 pair and the 0703 covering-grammar reference, and when I count the full population the band does not survive.

audits.the_argument: Two-part record. The ORIGINAL arm (turn_far_thinning = far-ladder change reads the running turn) was tested on the S95 fingerprint pass and DEMOTED to noise - a real falsification, executed, recorded, and the play rewritten around it. I reproduced that demotion off research/kalshi/renders/ng_refine_s95/fingerprints.json: across all 6,358 committed legs, legs that CONTINUED carry a 37.4% negative-turn_far_thinning share and legs that FADED carry 30.7%. A 6.7-point separation on n=6,358 is not a discriminator, and the sign of the difference runs AGAINST the arm's original direction (the turning legs are the LESS far-thinned ones). The demotion was correct and if anything understated. The SURVIVING arm (old-swing continuation-collapse + negative turn_exhaustion + peaked_fast) rests on one named instance, 1008 old-swing up-legs 0/15, which reproduces EXACTLY: 20251008 carries 15 up legs and 0 continued, against 12 of 26 down legs continuing on the same day. That is an argued mechanism (the old swing stops recruiting before price turns) with a traced first instance, which is NOVEL_N1 by the rubric's own discriminator - not ASSERTED. What it is NOT is MECHANISM_VERIFIED: there is no base rate, no non-turn control day, and no measured hit-rate for the surviving arm on its own. The record itself scopes it further - the surviving measurement is the SAME quantity as chain_polarity_flip C2 and inherits C2's G11 false negative and the S100.3 finding that it is non-discriminating on the 0107/0120 tape class.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: YES, decisively, for the demoted arm - it was tested and it failed, and the play was rewritten to say so. That is the strongest single signal in this batch that the desk's measurements are real. audits.the_argument: Claim: in a running chain, a counter-chain intraday spike that ROUND-TRIPS (closes >=~60% off the counter extreme), especially on the best remaining counter-catalyst, means counter-side liquidity is exhausted and the next session runs hard chain-side. This is the only play in my batch whose arming quantity and whose consequence are BOTH independently measured and BOTH reproduce exactly. Off research/kalshi/renders/ng_refine_s95/: 20251210 intraday peak +1060 closing +370 (65% off) -> 20251211 -3970; 20251230 peak +1990 closing +180 (91% off) -> 20251231 -2630; 20251002 peak +900 closing -440 -> 20251003 -680; 20260113 peak +1190 closing +320 (73% off) -> 20260114 -2710. Four for four, exact to the dollar, spanning G4, G9 and G10. The arming input (the fade percentage) is computed from the realized curve and is NOT the thing being predicted; the consequence (next-day net) could have been any number. That is the definition of evidence that could have come out otherwise. || I ADDED A BASE RATE, because four selected pairs are still four selected pairs. Across every committed rt file I defined the arming condition mechanically - an up-spike of >=$500 that round-tripped >=60% and still closed positive - and got n=9, of which 6 delivered a DOWN next day, against an unconditional down-day base rate of 93/171 = 54%. 67% vs 54% on n=9 is weak on its own. But the three FAILURES are 20250908 (+120 next), 20250915 (+1200) and 20251006 (+1360), and all three sit inside UP swings - which is exactly the polarity condition the play requires and my mechanical screen ignored. Conditioned on the play's own down-chain polarity the record is 6 of 6. The play's own G11 note independently reaches the same conclusion from the other direction: the two G11 misses (0121, 0127) were fired against give-backs inside an UP chain, and the record says in terms 'the tell has never been tested at up-polarity'. audits.the_argument: A gap-ownership rung with a four-limb conjunction: (a) BOTH futures books at 1y short extremes (NYMEX MM pctile <=~12 AND ICE LD1 <=~3) with a climax add or first covering print, (b) price at/near the bleed low, (c) a bullish storage-trajectory catalyst, (d) THE WINDOW - curve_regime contango while storage phase is withdraw. Mechanism argued and physical: a saturated short book at the lows facing a storage catalyst has no marginal seller, and a headroom-bounded warm cut cannot refill it. || THE EVIDENCE IS A BACK-CHECK, WHICH IS THE RIGHT SHAPE - a 15-gap sweep of every walk anchor with ZERO false fires, naming for each anchor WHICH limb failed. That could have produced false fires and did not. I tested the structural core of it myself against the committed states: across ALL 192 day-rows in every grp*_state.json in the repo, limb (d) is true on exactly four - 20260301, 20260302, 20260308, 20260309, all in G14 - and 0301/0308 are the only Sunday/Monday ANCHORS anywhere in the corpus where it holds. The play's claim that these are its unique qualifying anchors is corroborated independently. The two gaps reproduce exactly off g14_rt.json: 0301 gap +720, 0308 gap +1220. || THE FORWARD RECORD IS DECLINES, AND THEY ARE GOOD ONES. G15 declined twice with named numbers (0313->0315: NYMEX 25.5/ICE 10.4 and backwardation; 0320->0322: phase flipped to injection at the 0319 print, NYMEX 50.0 despite ICE 2.83). G20/G22/G23 keep declining with the same discipline - G22 specialist B and D each write out which limb failed and by how much, D noting 'One of two is not the conjunction'. Six groups, zero mis-ownership. || THE HAIRLINE, and it is the only thing wrong with this play. Limb (a)'s NYMEX bar is written '<=~12'. Both supporting instances read 12.26. Under a strict <=12 the play's own two founding gaps FAIL its own bar, and they are admitted only by the tilde. A bar sited at the exact edge of its own support is fitted to its support - the mirror image of the D23 finding that the healthiest bars sit at the CENTRE of their distribution. It has cost nothing so far because limb (d) has gated everything anyway, but it is a latent value-keyed condition of exactly the kind D23 was opened to catch.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: YES, twice over. The 15-gap back-check is a genuine falsification opportunity - any anchor passing all four limbs and NOT delivering a counter-side gap would have refuted it, and the sweep names each failing limb rather than asserting a clean result. And the forward record is DECLINES with served numbers, which is the hardest kind of evidence to fake: a play that declines correctly when its limbs fail is being run honestly. My independent recomputation of limb (d) across 192 day-rows could have contradicted the 'only 0301/0308' claim and did not.

G19 ran with every blind day reset to cum 0; B then wrote an 'age-5 DOWN chain' against a realized five-session UP covering rally. Both halves are in the corpus: the label itself in research/kalshi/forecasts/g19_blind_round1/grp19_mbo_specialist_B.json ('inherited chain age 5 (mature, >=3)'), and its refutation in research/kalshi/forecasts/grp19_postmortem_B.json ('The age-5 DOWN chain was fiction: the realized chain was a five-session UP covering rally (2.750 -> 3.019 open)... The inherited cum at 0515 close was +2110 (g19_actual.json), so the contradiction is arithmetic, not interpretive. The brain's 'corroborated by all five post-mortems' is prose citing prose - per the instance-discipline rule that is ONE instance, not five. || THE PLAY HAS CHANGED BEHAVIOUR, VISIBLY AND WIDELY, which is more than most process rules achieve. MANDATORY WARNING per boundary.chain_label_must_track_realized_cum: this label has NO realized cum behind it... The moment the next owner sees realized cum, RE-DERIVE and OVERRULE me.' 0703 then delivered +410 against A's -160 - the label WAS wrong, and the rule had already flagged it. || AND THE PLAY CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON THE ONE POINT IT IS MOST EMPHATIC ABOUT. Its caveat says 'The masked-price case is NOT an exemption: chain STATE travels in the handoff, which is never masked.' That is false on the served state, and seven posteriors say so: E-0626 'boundary.chain_label_must_track_realized_cum requires REALIZED cum, which is price-masked'; B-0629 'price cum declared unknowable rather than invented' (substituting cumulative signed flow, -3,909 lots); E-0710 'flow-derived substitute; requires realized cum, which is masked'; B-0713 'cum masked + staleness-gated'. What survives, and is arguably the better rule, is DECLARE-YOUR-BASIS-AND-FLAG-IT-FOR-OVERRIDE. That is not what the entry says.

What has NOT been shown is that enforcement improves accuracy - the postmortem's 'the handoff would have flipped 0518 to UP' is a counterfactual, not a measurement, and no scored comparison of enforced vs unenforced runs exists.

audits.condition_can_change_state: Not a numeric bar - it is a consistency constraint, so the question becomes: is it EVALUABLE? Only partly, and this is the finding. Realized cum_from_anchor is price content and IS masked in the blind, so on the modern architecture the rule's own required input is absent for the runs that need it most. It IS available in the handoff files (forecasts/g*_he24_he1_handoffs.json carry chain_polarity, chain_age_sessions and cum_from_anchor_usd) for in-block boundaries, and it IS available to the refine. So the rule is fully evaluable on refine runs and in-block refine boundaries, partly evaluable on in-block blind days (flow-cum substitute, declared), and NOT evaluable at all on block-open days (0622, 0608: no prior-group handoff exists). Evidence field: 'B-0629: the tilt gate fed +871 gross and weighted the self-derived residual 0.10 - the sign correction in r1 was the blind's own rule fed a decontaminated input.' audits.the_argument: MECHANISM: a front-loaded capture means the move is already paid for and round-trips; a slow build is continuous repricing that holds. SUPPORT: a per-leg rate on the committed fingerprint store, and I reproduced it independently. Across all 108 days / 6,358 legs in renders/ng_refine_s95/fingerprints.json, legs with peaked_fast=true (time-to-peak <= 60s) fail to hold (retention < 0.5 at the 1800s horizon) on 1,234 of 1,246 = 99.0%; only 12 held. On the 6 pivotal days the brain names, 39 of 40 peaked_fast legs faded (the brain's '23/24' is a narrower subset of the same set). The relationship is MONOTONE across four time-to-peak buckets: hold rate 1.0% (0-60s) -> 5.8% (60-300s) -> 16.1% (300-900s) -> 59.2% (900-1800s). TWO QUALIFICATIONS THE RECORD DOES NOT MAKE. (a) The two limbs are not symmetric: the SPIKE-FADES limb is near-deterministic, but the GRIND-HOLDS limb is a minority outcome - non-peaked_fast legs hold only 1,915 of 5,112 = 37.5% pooled, and reach 59% only in the slowest bucket. 'A slow GRIND holds (ride)' overstates its own evidence. (b) Retention is measured at a fixed 1800s horizon, so a peak at 60s has 1,740s to decay while a peak at 1,700s has 100s; part of the gradient is definitional. The monotone ordering survives that, the 1%-vs-59% headline does not fully. THE CONTRADICTION: the play's scope says 'leg side + hold-vs-fade (intraday); NOT the day net', yet its G11 FORWARD-CONFIRMED line reads 'both sides HIT' on two DAY NETS - a quantity the play excludes by its own words, on a day it oversized 2.9x.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: YES, emphatically, and this is the strongest single measurement in the batch. The hold rate could have been flat across the four time-to-peak buckets, or inverted, or the 12 spike-legs that held could have been 400. It is monotone across 6,358 legs on 108 days, and I computed it from the raw fingerprint store rather than reading the claim. The G11 arm is the exception: 'both sides hit' on 2 day nets could not have falsified a leg-level shape claim in either direction, and it is credited to the play anyway.

audits.the_argument: The play sorts expected magnitude by day-condition: UP-size weekend-gap Monday, storage Thursday and swing-reversal/seam; DOWN-size thin-holiday and non-catalyst chop. The entire support is a CURATED LIST OF DAY NETS on the conditions the play names ('Mon: 1020 +2770, 0929 +1240...; Thu: 0918 -1560, 1002 +1360...'), against a shorter list of small non-catalyst days. There is no counted base rate anywhere in the record. I computed one from the actuals: across G17-G23 (70 scored days, 14 storage Thursdays, 14 Mondays), a storage Thursday exceeds its OWN block's median |day_move| on 8 of 14 = 57%, and a Monday on 8 of 14 = 57%. Thursday's MEAN |move| is 850 against 435-526 for the other day-classes, so the TAIL claim survives - but that mean is carried by two days (0528 +2100, 0709 -2050), and this desk's standing rule forbids leading with a mean. In the CDD block G22 the two storage Thursdays (0625 -60, 0702 0) were the two SMALLEST days of the block against a 575 median, a direct contradiction of the flagship up-size arm. The calibration history is a WIDENING TENT: every time an extreme cleared the band top, the response was a new band (s97_2 winter bands, s98_2 year-end amplifier) and never a falsification - the record's own forward line says 'FORWARD-FAILED in calibration on every block' and keeps the play. And the G11 note raises confidence 0.45 -> 0.5 because the play 'earned the SIDE' on 0119 - a DIRECTION result banked by a play whose declared target is magnitude, on a day it oversized 3x.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: MOSTLY NO. The exemplar lists are selected on the outcome they exist to explain; a big day on a catalyst condition is entered as evidence and a small one is not counted. Two things DID come out the other way and are honestly recorded - the G7 1111 Veterans Day refutation of the thin-holiday down-size (15x under, re-scoped to require no live weather catalyst) and the standing 'the band tops are low' admission. Those are real. But the core up-size claim has never been scored against a base rate, and when I score it, it is 57% - four points better than a coin flip on the split it implies.

The trigger is a categorical day-class sort, so it splits every block by construction - each 10-day block carries two storage Thursdays, two Mondays and roughly four non-catalyst sessions. audits.the_argument: A five-arm rhythm class (B1 crashes arrive single; B2 bounces run 1-2 days never 3; B3 bounce-death gives a full crash band; B4 in-chain confirming prints size down; B5 more small days), each arm supported by a curated list of day-pairs that fit it. n = 2 blocks in ONE winter. The falsification history is the whole story: the record says 'FORWARD-FAILED on G11' - B2 broke on 0119/0120/0121, which ran three days and ACCELERATED - and then RETAINS B2 with a boundary condition invented after the fact that exactly excludes the breaking instance ('it applies only while no C1 band-break has printed'). The s101_3 block then records a SECOND 3-day counter-run against a B2 call (0203-0205) and re-scopes B2 a second time ('B2 owns BLEED-RHYTHM bounces'; the rest becomes a new FED-RECOVERY band). Two refutations, two post-hoc narrowings, zero retirements. The one full-block forward test scored 6/12 direction with the BLOCK LEAN WRONG - the record's own note says 'the bleed frame carried a down polarity through a block whose intraday nets summed +12,690'. And the caveats concede the structural hole: 'the class has no exit condition - it was carried intact through a block that reversed'.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: THE ARM LISTS, NO - crashes_single, bounces_1_2_days, bounce_death_crash and small_day_prevalence are enumerations of the day-pairs that fit, drawn from the two blocks the class was written on. THE FORWARD TESTS, YES, AND THEY CAME OUT AGAINST IT TWICE - and both times the answer was a new boundary condition rather than a retirement or a scoped refutation. A rule that has never been allowed to fail is not a rule that has been tested.

audits.the_argument: MECHANISM, ARGUED AND PHYSICAL: 'below the baseload floor there is no near-window Bcf mass for a ramp to deliver', so when near-window (D0..D+3) max forecast gw-HDD is under ~13.5 the weather DELIVERY band has no authority and the day reverts to its residual co-condition class one rung down. The form is declared a STEP not a ratio, and both smooth alternatives were measured and rejected (vol-scaling breaks G12 0203 at 3.3x; a headroom ratio leaves 0305 out) - that is a real functional-form comparison. There is a genuine NEGATIVE CONTROL and I verified it: every winter delivery-band day clears the gate. Computed off the served state, near-window max forecast gw-HDD is above the void bar on 12/12 days in each of G11, G12 and G13. BUT THE HEADLINE POSITIVE NUMBER IS FITTED. The evidence line reads '0305: near-window 13.4 max, call +550 vs actual +470' - and that +550 is the G14 REFINE-v2 number, produced on the block the play was derived from with the actual in hand; that pass ran 12/12 with every single day inside ~200 of actual. The G14 BLIND had 0305 at -900 against +470. The genuine forward instances are G15's 0319 and 0322, and there the record credits SIGN on a play whose target is MAGNITUDE: 0319 -800 vs -1080 (35% under) and 0322 -200 vs -930 (4.6x under). The one recorded mis-application, 0318 at -400 against +1900, was answered with a scoping caveat and 'Confidence unchanged - the gate is sound'.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: SPLIT. The winter negative control could have failed and did not - that is a real out-of-sample check across three blocks and I reproduced it. The functional-form rejection is a real comparison. The FOUNDING INSTANCE could not have come out otherwise: it was produced by a refine pass that fit every day of the block to within ~200. So the play has a tested boundary and an untested centre.

audits.the_argument: The play decomposes a Friday close into one of four exit types and has the weekend consume the TYPE rather than the day-net. Its own data_gap field is the confession: 'last-hour signed flow (field #3, the covering/exhaustion tell) is MBO-measured only for G15; for the rest of the record exit-type was inferred from archetype+curve-dir+calendar.' Inferring a type from the archetype - which is written after the Monday is known - is the S108 signature exactly: the label is fitted to the outcome and then the mechanism is credited. The evidence line ('POSITIONING_SPENT: 0327...; ROLL-CARRY: 0206 -> 0209...; FUNDAMENTAL_CARRY: 1128 -> 1201...') is a list of pairs that fit, one per type. I MADE TWO MEASUREMENTS THE RECORD NEVER DID, using the committed exit_states now available for G20-G23. (1) THE LABEL DOES NOT SURVIVE THE PRICE REVEAL. On the eight weekend-feeding Fridays of G20-G23 the refine CHANGED the blind's exit_type on SIX: 0529 (positioning_loaded_carry -> FLOWLESS_BID_WITHDRAWAL -> PASSIVE_LADDER_DISPLACEMENT, renamed twice), 0612 (POSITIONING_SPENT_FADE -> MOMENTUM_CARRY), 0619 (POSITIONING_CARRY -> MOMENTUM_CARRY, 'a correction of my own blind label'), 0626 (MOMENTUM_CARRY -> POSITIONING_SPENT_FADE), 0710 and 0717. Only 0605 and 0703 survived. (2) THE FOUR TYPES DO NOT SPAN THE SPACE. Three of the eight refine labels are outside the taxonomy entirely and the specialist says so each time: 'a fifth type, not one of the four in daytype.friday_exit_decomposition'; 'not any of the four labels the blind ruled out'; 'a THIRD exit form, not either of the two my lens file names'. Across all day-classes in G20-G23 the handoff_out record carries at least fourteen distinct non-canonical labels from four specialists (A, B, D and E).
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: NO for the record's own evidence - a type inferred from archetype+curve-dir after the fact cannot fail, because the archetype is itself written from the outcome. YES for the two measurements I ran, and they came out against the play: 2-of-8 blind label survival and 3-of-8 labels outside the taxonomy are both results that could have come out 8-of-8 and 0-of-8. The play's structural fix - 'Monday inherits the MEASURED exit-state, never the Friday label' - is sound doctrine, but the thing actually emitted at the open is a label, and the label is not stable.
