audits.the_argument: MECHANISM: a thin overnight book can print a gap on flow that does not confirm it; that gap is a head-fake, and the 06-10 ET catch-up window is where the inherited D-1 tilt reasserts. The call is a pure DIRECTION GATE - 'do NOT inherit the overnight gap sign' - and it sizes nothing. The founding n=2 is MBO-measured and I reproduced it to the digit off the committed evidence: 0316 has high_exc +490 with turn_down at 02:21, phase-0 signed flow -493 against a +230 price move, then phase-1 pxchg -930; 0323 has high_exc +1270, turn at 03:52, phase-0 sflow -26 against +1140, then phase-1 -1920. Those are exactly the record's numbers, and the flow tell is a quantity independent of the day net - it is not the outcome restated. THE FORWARD TEST THE RECORD STILL CALLS PENDING HAS NOW RUN AND IT PASSES. The brain says 'forward_evidence: NONE - proposed S104; G17+ is the forward test', and G17 through G23 have all been walked without anyone scoring it. Measured across those seven blocks: on the 14 Mondays with a non-zero overnight gap, the gap sign matches the regular-session net sign on only 5 = 36%; on the same Mondays the inherited D-1 (prior session) net sign matches on 8 of 13 = 62%. The play's exact claim - drop the gap sign, keep the inherited bias - wins the head-to-head 62% to 36%.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: YES, on both halves. The founding instances could have shown ph0 flow CONFIRMING the gap and the gap holding; they show the opposite twice with the reversal magnitudes recorded. The forward test could have come out at 64% for the gap sign instead of 36%. HONEST LIMIT, which the record should carry: n=14 and p(<=5 of 14 same | fair coin) = 0.21, so the gap-sign result alone is not significant in isolation; the 62%-vs-36% separation on the same Mondays is the stronger read, and it is still n=13.

audits.the_argument: MECHANISM, AND IT IS A STOCK-VS-FLOW ARGUMENT RATHER THAN AN OUTCOME RESTATEMENT: a covering give-back discharges a STOCK of crowded shorts, so the same still-extreme-but-not-worsening COT cannot arm it a second time; only a freshly rebuilt stack can. That makes a directional prediction that can fail, and the discriminator is a served, continuously-varying quantity (COT WoW) read across the specialist's own handoff seam. ORIGIN: G17 0417 fired covering-UP correctly (+40 actual); the blind then RE-FIRED it on 0424 (+250 guess against -380 actual) and the test-drive reverted 0424 to DOWN while leaving 0417 intact. THE RECORD UNDERSTATES ITSELF - it stops at G18, and I found three more clean resolutions. G18 0508 is the cleanest single instance because grp18_blind_E.json carries it as a STRUCTURED rule record with inputs, thresholds, scope_pass and a magnitude band: cot_chg_wow +3,329 (not worsening) -> re-fire declined -> band [-700,-150] -> actual -360, in band and right sign, in the BLIND. G21 carries BOTH LIMBS IN ONE BLOCK: the 06-09 COT printed MM -122,617, WoW -7,763, 1-year percentile 2.83 - a fresh worsening extreme - inside E's 0612 session, and 0615 delivered +910 with absorb_session TRUE and ph3 -1,451 absorbed under +520, which is textbook covering; the SAME report at age 6.35 days on 0619 was declared spent fuel and not re-fired, and 0619 delivered -110. G22 0626: WoW +2,187, percentile 29.25, not a new extreme and not worsening -> covering-UP explicitly un-licensed. G23 0710: WoW +17,914 improving -> 'covering-UP not fired and explicitly not re-fired'.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: YES, and G21 is the case that makes it - the SAME instrument armed a covering delivery when it was fresh (0615, +910 with absorption confirmed) and declined it when the same report was stale (0619, -110), in one block, with the two outcomes going the two different ways. THE WEAKNESS I MUST NAME: the DECLINE branch resolves to 'the chain/state default', so when the play stands down it makes no independent claim and a wrong decline is charged to the chain rather than to this play. Only the G17 0424 origin, the G18 0508 banded call and the G21 0615 fresh-limb fire are scoreable in their own right.

audits.the_argument: MECHANISM: where a session CLOSED in its range is a statement about who is holding inventory at the bell, whereas a declining final-phase signed-flow COUNT can equally mean a handover - so take the continuation verdict from close LOCATION, not from flow-shape decay. The brain's own G20 0529 measurement is the sharpening: ph3 was the session's LARGEST phase by volume by 18% (60,930 lots) on a net of only -59, so the prose 'the covering bid went home' described participation and participation was maximal - hence the (VOLUME, NET) pair refinement, objected by B, conceded by E, verified independently by A. THE FOUNDING n=2 REPRODUCES on committed evidence: 0514 close_off_low ~0.86 with phase sflow 118 -> 913 -> 41 (the exact '913 -> 41 decay' the record names) and the next session +320; 0515 close_off_low ~0.76 and Monday 0518 +660. Both closed high on decaying flow and both continued. I THEN RAN THE FORWARD TEST THE RECORD ONLY PROMISES ('rides G20+ Fridays'), off the committed exit_states: on the seven weekend-feeding Fridays of G20-G23, sign(close_off_low_frac - 0.5) predicts the next session's net on 5 of 7; on the tighter >=0.70 / <=0.30 bar it is 4 of 5. THE HEAD-TO-HEAD THE PLAY ACTUALLY ASSERTS COMES OUT ITS WAY: on those same seven Fridays, last-hour SIGNED-FLOW sign predicts 2 of 7 and last-hour PRICE direction 3 of 7. And it is properly a PER-CELL result: pooled over all 40 days carrying exit_states the same bar is 13 of 25 = 52%, a coin flip. The edge lives in the Friday cell, which is the play's declared scope.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: YES, and this is the only play in the batch whose central claim is a HEAD-TO-HEAD against a named alternative on the same days. The comparator (flow shape) could have beaten close location and did not - 2/7 against 5/7 on the identical seven Fridays. The pooled-vs-Friday contrast (52% vs 71-80%) could also have come out the other way, showing a general effect that the Friday scope was needlessly narrowing; instead it confirms the scope. HONEST LIMIT: n = 5 to 7. p(4+ of 5 | fair coin) = 0.19, so no single one of these is significant alone; the pattern across three comparators on the same days is what carries it.

audits.the_argument: This is a META-RULE about how other plays' limbs evaluate, and it is a genuine conditional rule with a trigger, a read and a call, so it is a play and not a descriptor. MECHANISM: an unreachable absolute bar must return UNKNOWN, never a satisfied/refuted boolean - and the specific harm named is that a '<=' bar and a '>=' bar on the SAME unreachable quantity both degrade in the SAME direction (one voids the weather band, the other silently defaults a selector bearish), so several nominally independent artifacts are one artifact wearing several hats. I VERIFIED BOTH BARS IT NAMES BY ID, independently, off the served state. selector.divergence_resolution's gw_hdd >= 16.4: fires 12/12 in G11, 12/12 in G12, then 0/11 in G16 and 0/10 in each of G18, G19, G20, G21, G22, G23 - degenerate in 9 of the 12 blocks with served weather, splitting only G13 (9/12), G14 (4/12) and G15 (3/12). magnitude.shoulder_weather_band_void's near-window <= 13.5: 0/12 in G11, G12 and G13, then 10/10 in every one of G18 through G23 - also degenerate in 9 of 12, splitting only G14, G15 and G16. So the claim 'four independent HDD-keyed artifacts all degraded bearish-or-void in one CDD block' is measurably true on the two bars it names. ITS FALSIFIER IS STATED AND IT SURVIVES: in G11 and G12 the regime is HDD-dominant (D0 gw_hdd 20-41 against gw_cdd 0.0-0.9), so the play is inert there exactly as it claims it must be.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: YES. Either bar could have split its blocks and neither does - 12/12 and 0/10 are the two ways a threshold can be dead, and both bars produce both, in opposite seasons. This is a rate measurement across twelve blocks, not an exemplar list, and it is reproducible from committed state in one pass. The one thing the record leans on that I would not count is the signed-error attribution ('the blind's four down-calls-that-printed-up contributed -3,840 of a -1,815 drift') - that is an outcome decomposition and it could not have falsified the mechanism.

audits.the_argument: MECHANISM, GENUINELY ARGUED: a void is price discovering where liquidity sits; once found, flow stops moving price, so a numb terminal phase (k3 = |ph3 price change| / |ph3 signed flow| <= 0.05 on >= 500 lots) carries into the next session's NET but not into its RANGE. The record is the most disciplined-LOOKING in the batch - it declares D24 state (a) verbatim, names a base rate, names one counterexample and refuses to explain it away, flags its own boundary instance at 489 lots against a 500 floor, and measures the net-vs-range corollary separately. I REPRODUCED ITS ARITHMETIC EXACTLY off renders/ng_refine_s95/g23_mbo_evidence.json: 0710 k3 = 0.3021, 0713 = 0.0258, 0714 = 0.0177, which is the record's '0.302 -> 0.026 -> 0.018'; 0703's ph3 flow is -489, which is the declared 2% boundary miss. Applying the play's own bar to G20 and G23 reproduces n=6 and 5/6 at <= $200 to the day. THEN THE DEFECT: the same phases data exists for all SEVEN blocks G17-G23 and the search stopped at two. Extending the IDENTICAL test to all 70 scored days gives TWELVE numb seams, of which 5 land at <= $200 - a 42% rate against a 24% base rate, not 5-of-6. And the split is total: the five hits are ALL in G20 and G23, while the six seams in G17, G18 and G19 are 0-FOR-6, with next-day |net| of 380, 420, 1230, 720, 360 and 420 (median 420). audits.the_argument: Two arms. (a) MAGNITUDE: a big |stor_surprise| implies a bigger-leg day, near-consensus implies range/chop. (b) SIGN: the surprise sign does NOT sort direction. The entire evidence field is `distinct_prints: 6` - a count of the SAMPLE, not a measurement of the EFFECT - plus one exemplar, 0820, which is a counterexample supporting arm (b)'s negative claim rather than support for arm (a). No mechanism is argued for why surprise magnitude should scale the leg; the `call` field restates the rule. The forward field is candid: NEGATIVE-TO-INERT, and the magnitude arm is 'subsumed by daytype.storage_thursday_magnitude'. I MEASURED THE MAGNITUDE ARM. stor_surprise is served on 40 days across grp20-grp23_state.json (g18 and g19 carry it null on every day - the S107 empty-storage hole). corr(|stor_surprise|, |day_move_usd|) = 0.087 on n=40. Split at 10 Bcf: |surp|>=10 gives mean |dm| 648 / median 520 (n=10); |surp|<10 gives mean 554 / median 610 (n=30) - the mean lifts trivially and the MEDIAN runs backwards. On the 9 first-served days (the day a new surprise becomes open-time knowable) the two largest surprises, 33.0 and 39.2, delivered 620 and 410, while 9.4 delivered 1,340; r = 0.255 on n=9. SEPARATELY, AND MORE SERIOUSLY, THE INSTRUMENT IS THE WRONG QUANTITY: `read` says '|stor_surprise| (Bcf vs seasonal)' and the served field is indeed vs the 5-year norm, while the market prices vs CONSENSUS, which the same state block serves as storage_consensus.next_print.consensus_chg_bcf.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: The record's own evidence, NO. 'distinct_prints: 6' cannot fail - it is the sample size. The one exemplar is a refutation of the sign arm, so it is evidence AGAINST a different arm, not evidence FOR this one. My measurement, YES, and it came out flat: an r of 0.087 on 40 days with the big-surprise median BELOW the small-surprise median is exactly what a null looks like. Arm (b), the negative claim that the sign does not sort, IS supported by the same data and could have failed: across g20-g23 the 20 days served an 'above' (bearish) surprise closed up 12 times and the 19 scorable days served a 'below' (bullish) surprise closed up 8 times - the fundamental sign is if anything inverted, so the negative claim survives.

audits.the_argument: A real mechanism is argued: a counter-swing (give-back) that exhausts lets the underlying swing resume, one that does not exhaust continues. The support is a very large per-event narrative in which the close-recovery fraction and the outcome are read together, day by day, and the play itself concedes the parameters were read off those outcomes - 'Thresholds (~40-50% recovery) are descriptive bands, not fitted constants.' EVERY COUNTEREXAMPLE PRODUCED A NEW ARM RATHER THAN A REFUTATION, six times: S97.2 added a ramp arm and a depth arm; G9 added polarity-relativity after the blind misapplied it up-side three times; S98.2 added a bounce-never-extends asymmetry; S99.2 added chain-side-days-only plus a bleed override; S102.2 added the flow-absorption arm. THE RECORD CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON ONE DAY: forward_evidence calls G11 0129 'a clean forward hit' (resume called, +1,480 actual) while legacy_notes.g11_note says the play 'fired twice, both directions missed - 0126 -620a vs +500g and 0129 +1480a vs -1800g'. Both cannot be true of the same fire; the resolution is that the 'forward hit' is a refine-time re-application with the outcome visible, and the field does not say so. AVAILABILITY: the primary close-vs-extreme arm needs day-N-1 realized price and is stood down by construction in every modern blind - I verified explicit stand-downs in grp22_B_20260622, grp22_B_20260629, grp22_D_20260625 and grp23_C_20260707 - and it appears in NO refine posterior for g19-g23. So the primary arm has zero evaluations anywhere in the modern corpus. I THEREFORE MEASURED THE ONE BLIND-AVAILABLE ARM, the S102.2 flow-absorption turn (big_print_b_share >= ~0.62 AND session_b_share <= ~0.45), across all 60 served sessions of g18-g23: it fires 3 times, on 1, 6 and 2 big prints. Every fire is a degenerate thin-tape reading of exactly the kind flow.big_print_bshare_thin_tape_guard exists to stand down. On well-sampled tape (big_prints_n >= 20) it is 0 of ~50 - the 0.62 bar sits above the entire thick-tape distribution in six blocks. TO THE PLAY'S CREDIT, ITS DERIVATION REPRODUCES EXACTLY: grp15_state.json serves the 0317 session under key 20260318 at big_print_b_share 0.643 / session_b_share 0.413 (the founding fire, +1,900), and all four named non-fires reproduce to three decimals (0319 0.593, 0322 0.542, 0324 0.373, 0325 0.174). But the founding fire itself sits on 14 big prints, inside the thin quartile.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: The narrative evidence, NO. Once a break can be reclassified into a new arm - ramp, depth, polarity, bleed, chain-side-only - no day can refute the play, and the record is a history of exactly that reclassification. The G11 entry shows the mechanism operating in miniature: two recorded direction misses were re-attributed to 'a known-degraded input, not a test of the read with tape.' MY ARM-LEVEL MEASUREMENT, YES, and it could easily have returned a bar that splits days sensibly; instead it returned 3 fires in 60 sessions, all degenerate.

audits.the_argument: The mechanism is stated crisply and it is checkable: the market prices a weather shot ONCE, so a FIRST APPEARANCE at a previously empty horizon carries information while a REVISION to an already-priced shot does not. The mechanism instance is specific and traced: the 0125 cut (-2.315 at Jan 30) and the 0126 re-add (+3.197 at the same target) cancel to approximately nothing within two runs - 'which is the definition of noise on a priced event, and is the mechanism.' WHAT MAKES THIS ONE DIFFERENT FROM THE REST OF MY BATCH IS THAT IT MEASURED ITSELF AND PAID FOR IT. The s101_3 block scores four G12 uses individually, with two flat MISSES named as misses (0202, 0204) and one scored 'day-net MISS / regime-trajectory HIT'; the probation_resolution then records the first-appearance arm as '0/3 forward as a STANDALONE day-net side caller' and DEMOTES it. A play that writes down its own 0/3 and acts on it is doing the thing this audit is looking for. It also derived a replacement with named n - the s101_6 PRICING-TIME rule (shock adds >= ~3-4 gw-HDD price at appearance, n=2; moderate adds price on entering D+0..D+2, n=1 sequence, back-checked against 1109 and 1123). WHERE IT IS NOW STALE: the surviving revision-inert arm is recorded as 'unchanged, still harmless', and that claim rests on four G12/G13 NON-uses, which cannot hurt by construction. It is contradicted twice in G22, both times by the specialist who fired it. On 0624 C read forecast_run_delta_cdd -0.011 as inert and held the sign DOWN at -200 into a +800 day; C's own refine diagnosed it exactly - 'the target-date forecast never moved; the mass ROLLED DOWN into D0 by the passage of time. forecast_run_delta_cdd measures revisions and is blind to roll-down.' On 0630 C fired the same arm ('the +0.261 gw CDD add sits at horizons the heat has occupied since 0626, so it is inert as a side caller and does not flip the sign') and guessed -420 into a +780 day. The correction C proposed - roll-down is not a revision - is NOT in the brain: the string 'roll-down' appears zero times in knowledge/ng_brain.json.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: YES, AND IT DID. The first-appearance arm's forward record came out against it (0/3) and the record demoted the arm rather than rescuing it - that is a measurement that falsified a claim and was acted on, which is the discriminator for this class. The weaker half is the revision-inert arm, whose support is '4/4 harmless' non-uses; a non-use cannot fail, so that specific evidence could NOT have come out otherwise, and the two G22 instances above are what a real test of it looks like.

In g21-g23 there is no cold shot to rise, so the limb is 0-of-30 by construction - this is a WINTER instrument, and the play says so ('a cold-shot appearance/repricing day'). Limb (iii) does change state cleanly: COT MM 1y pctile across g18-g23 runs 0.94 to 50.0 and clears the <=12 bar on 30 of 60 days. So the play is not dead, it is out of season: the conjunction cannot fire until a heating block is staged, and G24 needs a data pull rather than a re-stage.
audits.falsifier: The record's own words are the falsifier and they are still unmet: 'the 1.35 bottom bound IS 0311's own print... the bound needs G15+ forward evidence' and 'forward_evidence: NONE'. The concrete test: on the next block where limb (i) can fire (a heating block with far-window HDD rising two cycles) and limbs (ii)/(iii) hold, record the band top and the multiplier BEFORE the day. A realized multiplier outside [1.35, 2.55], or a fire on a day that delivers inside the ordinary band, refutes the band. A second, cheaper falsifier for the trigger: any day satisfying all three limbs that does NOT exceed its band top.

audits.the_argument: The play was written to explain a known set of bad outcomes, and it says so in its own caveats: 'This is the mechanism that explains the worst Monday reversals that followed a CORRECT Friday direction.' Its evidence is four named days, each described in the hindsight form 'the driver realized over the weekend and the Monday reversed' or 'the driver was still ahead and the Monday carried' - 0220/0405 for the REALIZING arm, 1128/0111 for the AHEAD arm. There is no count, no base rate over all weekend seams, and no out-of-sample check. forward_evidence at merge read 'NONE - proposed S104; G17+ is the forward test'. I TRACED THE FORWARD TEST AND IT IS 1-OF-4 ON SIGN. Both arms failed in G22, each diagnosed by its own author in the refine. On 0703 A fired the REALIZING arm ('the driver's peak is LANDING, not AHEAD - which is the sell-the-news arm') for guessed_net -160 against +410; A's refine calls it 'one FIXABLE miss (carry_realization_flip's realizing arm applied to a slope-class driver)'. On 0629 B fired the AHEAD arm ('the driver's peak is still AHEAD of Monday (h1 CDD 15.933 > h0 14.815), so Monday CARRIES... Keeps the session shallow') for guessed_net +325 against -1,110; B's refine says the arm was 'applied at the WRONG LEVEL: peak-ahead is true of GROSS CDD, but the tradeable object is the burn RESIDUAL, which had already flipped negative (-4.2 Bcf/d).' AFTER the S110 scope split the CARRY arm fired twice more in G23: 0706 guessed +500 against +100 (sign right) and 0713 guessed +550 against -620 (sign wrong, error 1,170). A RECORD-VERSUS-POSTERIOR MISMATCH: scope_split_s110 says applying the REALIZING arm to a slope-class driver 'produced the 0703 blind miss and 0629's gap call'. But grp22_B_20260629.json shows B fired the AHEAD arm, not the realizing arm, and its refine attributes the failure to the SESSION (blind -155 vs -1,160, error 1,005 - explicitly 'the larger failure') via gross-versus-residual, not to the gap (error 430). The merged scope split names the wrong arm and the wrong leg for 0629, and the residual-versus-gross correction B actually proposed is not in the play at all.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: NO on the founding evidence. The discriminator - whether the driver's peak 'realized over the weekend' or was 'still ahead' - is assigned retrospectively on days already selected for having reversed or carried, so the four exemplars cannot fail. It is the classic explain-the-misses construction and the play states that purpose openly. The forward record CAN fail and did: 3 wrong signs in 4 traced fires, including one after the play had already been scoped once.

audits.condition_can_change_state: YES, AND THE DISCRIMINATOR IS COMPUTABLE FROM SERVED STATE. The test 'is the driver's peak ahead of Monday or landing over the weekend' reads off weather_forecast.horizons, which is served on every day of g18-g23 and moves freely - across the four g22/g23 weekend seams the h0-to-h1 CDD step alone runs -0.9 to +1.4 and the D+3 peak location changes week to week. The S110 shot-versus-slope test ('is the driver IN the forward ladder at the exit') is also computable. So this play does not have the degenerate-bar problem; its problem is that the computable condition does not sort the outcome (1 of 4 forward). One caveat on attribution: on 0706 and 0713 the play is one input among six or seven in B's stack, so the sign is not attributable to it alone; on 0703 and 0629 the authors attribute the miss to it themselves in their own refine posteriors, which is clean.
audits.falsifier: None written. The obvious one, which the corpus can already run: over all 12 weekend seams in g18-g23, classify each Friday's driver as REALIZING or AHEAD from weather_forecast.horizons known at the Friday close, then score the Monday day_move sign. Anything at or below chance refutes it. The traced fires give 1-of-4 already. A second, sharper test comes from B's own refine and is not in the play: run the peak-ahead test on the burn RESIDUAL (grid_stack est_gas_burn net of wind/solar) rather than gross CDD, and check whether the 0629 sign flips. If it does, the play needs a residual limb before it may be applied in a renewables-heavy summer regime.

audits.the_argument: The rule is that Monday's direction comes from the inherited D-1 (Friday+Sunday) trade tilt - E.monday_bias / C.conviction_verdict - and not from the gap sign or the Friday day-net, with the catch-up window confirming or fading it. THE HEADLINE SUPPORT IS A 4/4 COMPUTED IN THE REFINE WITH THE OUTCOMES VISIBLE, AND THE PLAY CONTRADICTS IT IN ITS OWN RECORD. forward_evidence_g21_leg_vs_day says the gate 'Calls the Monday DAY-MOVE sign 4/4 on the walk's four scorable weekend seams' and names 0518, 0601, 0608, 0615 through its leg examples. The assumption_retired block in the SAME play record says of 0601: 'Consulting this gate on the state actually served REPRODUCES +350' - against a realized -990. A day cannot be both a 4/4 member and a reproduction of the blind's wrong sign. I CHECKED THE BLIND RECORD ON ALL FOUR: 0518 -550 vs +660 (wrong), 0601 +350 vs -990 (wrong), 0608 -420 vs -890 (right), 0615 +320 vs +160 (right) - 2 of 4, not 4 of 4. Across the six Mondays that ran AFTER the Monday prior-session stub defect was fixed (g21 restaged onward) the gate's owner B went 3 of 6 on sign: 0608 right, 0615 right, 0622 -420 vs +650 wrong, 0629 +325 vs -1,110 wrong, 0706 +500 vs +100 right, 0713 +550 vs -620 wrong. THE DEEPER PROBLEM IS THAT THE GATE'S INPUT IS AN AGENT OUTPUT. Its `read` names E.monday_bias and C.conviction_verdict - labels produced by other specialists in the same run, after their own decontamination and taxonomy judgments - not a served field. So the 4/4 cannot be recomputed by anyone, and the same tape can be handed to the gate as UP or DOWN depending on how the upstream specialist wrote its handoff. When I substitute the nearest served proxy (the sign of the Friday's session_signed_flow from tape_conditions.prior_full_session) the gate calls the Monday day-move sign 5 of 9 clean Fridays - a coin flip. WHAT IS GOOD IN THE RECORD: the assumption_retired block is a model of the correction this audit wants. It withdraws a 'failed to consult' verdict, names the actual cause (session 20260529 appears on no day; the Monday was served the Sunday reopen stub with signed flow +278 in place of the Friday's -2,126 on ~117,069 lots), and credits the specialist who was right. I verified the stub from grp20_state.json: the 0601 entry serves session 20260531, 1 big print, 1,224 trades.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: The 4/4, NO - it is a refine-time re-application of a rule whose input is another agent's label, scored against days whose outcomes were already known, and one of the four is a day the same record says the gate gets wrong on the served state. The assumption_retired measurement, YES - B audited tape_conditions.session across all ten G20 days and could have found the Friday present; it found it absent on every day. My proxy test, YES, and it came out at chance.

audits.condition_can_change_state: THE SERVED HALF YES, THE DECIDING HALF NO. tape_conditions.prior_full_session is populated on every post-fix Monday and its Friday signed flow ranges -3,916 to +3,189 with two-sided b_share 0.433-0.520 across the twelve Mondays of g18-g23, so a served-tilt version of the gate would change state freely. But the play does not key on the served field - it keys on E.monday_bias / C.conviction_verdict, which are AGENT OUTPUTS produced later in the same run, after decontamination and taxonomy judgments that are not recorded as numbers. That is a category of unfalsifiability the batch rubric does not name: the condition can take any state the upstream specialist gives it, so no state file can ever contradict the gate. Two of the twelve Mondays additionally served a Sunday stub (0525, 0601) and one served a Juneteenth half session (0622), so three of twelve had a structurally degraded input.
audits.falsifier: None written. Two are needed and both are runnable today. (1) PIN THE INPUT: restate the gate on a SERVED quantity - sign(prior_full_session.session_signed_flow) or two-sided b_share versus 0.50 - and score the Monday day-move sign over the twelve seams in g18-g23. I ran the signed-flow form on the nine Mondays with a real Friday and got 5 of 9; the two-sided b_share form gives 3 of 6 where it is served. (2) RE-SCORE THE 4/4 HONESTLY: recompute the four named seams from the blind record rather than from the refine, which gives 2 of 4, and say in the field which round produced the number. Until (1) exists, no observation can refute this play, because any miss can be attributed to the upstream bias having been wrong - which is what happened on both 0601 and 0629.

audits.the_argument: The claim is that signed-flow-versus-price CONVICTION (absorption), not raw imbalance, is the direction discriminator: sell flow absorbed under a rising price is crowded-short covering and delivers UP, buy flow absorbed under a falling price is failing and stays DOWN, aligned flow delivers in its own direction. EVERY NUMBER IN THE EVIDENCE FIELD REPRODUCES EXACTLY from g18_mbo_evidence.json and g18_actual.json - 0501 total_sflow -3,358 with day_move +280 and absorb_session true; 0508 total_sflow -3,214 with day_move -370 and absorb_session false; the 'near-identical -3300 flow, opposite signs' pairing is real; 0427 +370 and 0504 +610 with gap +440; the C mirror 0429/0505/0506 all carry positive total_sflow with negative day_move and absorb_session true. The derivation is honest and traceable. THE PROBLEM IS THAT THE DISCRIMINATOR IS COMPUTED FROM THE OUTCOME. absorb_session and ph_absorb are flags derived from flow-versus-realized-price disagreement, so 'sell flow ABSORBED under a rising price delivered UP' is very close to a restatement of what the flag means. The play concedes the dependency in its requires field ('signed flow + price by phase (refine/live)') and its evidence line makes the credit explicit: 'The refine flipped every one; the price-walled blind (which sees flow but not price) called them the raw-imbalance way and missed.' All of its evidence is from G18, the block it was derived on. I TESTED THE ONE FORWARD-FACING FORM. The `call` contains a genuine next-session claim: a crowded short (MM 1y pctile < ~12) whose covering is absorbed at the Friday close reprices UP on the Monday catch-up. Across the eleven Fridays of g18-g23 the crowded-short SELL-absorbed branch fires exactly ONCE - 0501, MM pctile 8.49, final-phase absorption true, sell flow -3,358 - and that fire is the in-sample founding instance. It never arms again: 0508/0515/0605/0612/0619 carry no final-phase absorption; 0529 (16.04), 0626 (25.47), 0703 (29.25) and 0710 (44.34) fail the crowded-short gate outright; and the one other armed Friday, 0522, is the MIRROR branch (buy flow +349 absorbed, MM 0.94, so 'stays down') and its Monday 0525 came in +30, i.e. flat rather than down. Generalizing to 'does absorb_session on day D call day D+1' across g18-g23 gives 8 of 18 - a coin flip. TO ITS CREDIT, the play carries an S108-signature self-correction inside it: assumption_retired_timing_limb withdraws D's pre-print timing claim after the per-leg check refuted it 1 of 4, and names the disease exactly - 'G20 credited the generator from DAY NETS; the intraday check was never run.'
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: MOSTLY NO. The flag that does the sorting is built from the price the flag is used to predict, so on a same-session read the evidence is near-tautological; and the sample is one block, chosen because that block was a covering rally. What COULD have come out otherwise is the forward Friday-to-Monday arm, and it has never been given the chance - it arms once in six blocks and that once is in-sample. The retired timing limb is the exception that proves the record can measure honestly: a per-leg decomposition refuted it and the play recorded the refutation against its own author.

audits.condition_can_change_state: YES ON THE FLAG, NO ON THE GATE THAT MAKES IT TRADEABLE. absorb_session is true on 21 of the 60 days in g18-g23 and ph_absorb varies freely, so the absorption discriminator itself is far from degenerate. But the play's forward, blind-relevant form needs the crowded-short gate MM 1y pctile < ~12, and that gate has been UNREACHABLE since 20260622: COT MM 1y pctile reads 25.47 on 0623, 29.25 from 0629, 44.34 from 0707 and 50.0 from 0713, so across all twenty days of g22 and g23 the gate fires on exactly one (0622, at 2.83, on a stale report re-served at age 9.35 days). Specialists correctly stood it down for this reason - grp23_C_20260707 records 'MM 44.34 pctile is not crowded-short < ~12'. So the play is out of regime, not refuted; D31 applies.
audits.falsifier: None written, and this play needs one badly because its main flag is derived from the quantity it predicts. Two candidates. (1) FORWARD FORM, blind-legal: over all crowded-short Fridays (MM pctile < 12) in g18-g23, score whether final-phase absorption calls the Monday day-move sign. The arm fires once (0501 -> 0504, correct) and its aligned counterpart fires once (0508 -> 0511, wrong), which is 1-of-2 and not a test. (2) SEPARATE THE FLAG FROM THE OUTCOME: score absorb_session on day D against day D+1's direction, which does not reuse D+1's price. I ran it across g18-g23 and got 8 of 18 - at chance. A play whose discriminator is computed from realized price must be scored on a LATER day than the one that built it, and no evidence in this record does that.

audits.the_argument: A statistical mechanism is argued and then measured against it. big_print_b_share is a proportion, so its dispersion is governed by the number of big prints behind it; on a thin tape it wanders from 0.50 for purely sampling reasons and an absolute 0.55 bar silently becomes a looser bar. The record supplies counts, per-quartile dispersions, equal-fire-rate bars, a correlation, and a stated falsifier. I RE-RAN THE WHOLE MEASUREMENT from the committed 204-row dataset renders/ng_refine_s95/bshare_rows.json. Pooled: n=204 spanning 20251103-20260720, mean 0.461, sd 0.169, p50 0.479, 0.55 at the 72.5th percentile firing on 27.5% of sessions - EVERY ONE OF THOSE EXACT. Thinnest quartile (bigs 1-20, median 9): sd 0.255, fire rate 31.4% - both EXACT. The other three quartiles: my sd 0.134 / 0.119 / 0.126 against the record's 0.132 / 0.120 / 0.127. corr(|b_share - 0.50|, log big_prints_n) = -0.488 against the record's -0.465. The equal-rate bars and the fire-rate spread differ modestly with quartile-boundary handling (my fixed-bar spread 9.8pp against the record's 7.9pp; my guarded spread 7.8pp against 4.5pp), so the guard's benefit is somewhat smaller than recorded but the shape - a STEP confined to the thinnest quartile, flat across the other three - is exactly reproduced. MOST IMPORTANTLY THE RECORDED NEGATIVE RESULT REPRODUCES: the elegant 0.50 + k/sqrt(n) form is worse than the crude fixed bar at every k tested (my per-quartile spreads 19.6 / 23.5 / 23.5 / 17.6pp against a fixed-bar 9.8pp; the record's 18.5 / 22.4 / 22.3 / 16.3 against 7.9), and for the reason the record gives - it over-corrects the thick tail and ends up firing MOST on the thickest quartile. The record is also unusually honest about effect size: 'the guard is a modest, targeted correction - it is NOT a large effect and should not be sold as one.' ONE CLAIM IN THE FORWARD FIELD DOES NOT HOLD. The four-lens G20 note says Memorial Day 20260525 (0.599 on 13 big prints) 'is G20's only reading clearing 0.55'. On the committed size-weighted state, session 20260602 also reads 0.585 on 122 big prints - a thick tape that clears 0.55 and that the guard does not touch. The 0.599-on-13 number itself is exact, as is 'then came in -190' for 0526, and the degenerate Sunday-stub readings of exactly 1.0 on 1 big print (0524 at 658 trades, 0531 at 1,224 trades).
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: YES, DECISIVELY, AND PART OF IT DID. The thinnest quartile could have carried the same dispersion as the others - it carries double. The bar could have floated by season - the record tested that and found it does not (my recomputation: 25.3% winter, and the shoulder/summer split differs from the record's with a different month boundary but the conclusion is the same). And the author's preferred smooth form was tested FIRST and LOST badly to the crude one, and the loss was written down so nobody re-proposes it. That is the cleanest example of Result Discipline in the batch. The dataset is committed, so the measurement is re-runnable by anyone - which is exactly what I did.

audits.condition_can_change_state: YES, AND IT IS THE ONLY PLAY IN MY BATCH WHERE THE BAR IS SITED IN THE MIDDLE OF ITS OWN DISTRIBUTION. The gating quantity is big_prints_n, which across the 204-session dataset runs 1 to 387 with quartile boundaries at 20 / 48 / 87 - the <=20 condition selects 51 of 204 sessions, i.e. 25.0%, which is as far from degenerate as a bar gets. Within the served corpus it also splits blocks rather than whole blocks: g18-g23 carry 60 served readings of which 10 fall at or under 20 big prints, spread across five of the six blocks. This is the healthy form D23 describes - an absolute bar sited at the centre of its distribution rather than at an edge - and it is worth naming as the positive template, since three other plays in this batch fail exactly the opposite way.
audits.falsifier: WRITTEN, SPECIFIC, AND STILL UNRUN: 'If thin-tape sessions (big_prints_n < 20) that clear 0.55 but not 0.60 go on to deliver conviction-consistent direction at the same rate as thick-tape 0.55 fires, the guard is wrong and should be withdrawn.' The corpus can nearly run it now - the 204-row dataset gives the readings and the actuals give the outcomes for the g17-g23 subset - but the dataset carries no next-day direction column, so it needs a join before it can be scored. That join is the single cheapest upgrade available to any play in this batch. Separately, the forward field's 'G20's only reading clearing 0.55' should be corrected to name session 0602 (0.585 on 122 prints).

audits.the_argument: This is a DATA-HANDLING RULE about how to read a served field, not a market conditional. Its call - 'seam weather reads use LEVEL differences only; run deltas are intra-week instruments' - makes no claim about price, direction or magnitude, so no day-net observation can bear on it. It is also already served by the pipeline: weather_forecast_cycle.weekday_open.seam_delta_warning carries the identical instruction verbatim on EVERY day of grp22_state.json (I checked 0626, 0629 and 0630 - byte-identical text: 'run deltas baseline run-over-run, NOT session-over-session. Across a weekend/holiday seam use the LEVEL difference... never these deltas'). So the entry duplicates a warning string the state already prints, which makes it an A-7 / D30 question about where doctrine lives rather than a support-classification question. ITS TRACED INSTANCE IS EXACT. G22 0629: forecast_run_delta_cdd -0.219 against a D0 CDD level rise of 14.815 - 10.076 = +4.739 (the record says +4.7); and 'mechanism verified on 0624 (level +2.205, field -0.011)' reproduces to three decimals (10.022 - 7.817 = 2.205; d_gw_cdd h0 = -0.011). If Greg rules that instrument-reading rules ARE plays, then on the evidence this is a NOVEL_N1 with a partial refutation, and I would not argue with that reading - I am classifying on what the entry IS, not on how well it is evidenced. TWO SUBSTANTIVE PROBLEMS EITHER WAY. (1) The stated mechanism - across a multi-cycle seam 'the channel is STRUCTURALLY ~ZERO' - does not hold on the corpus's other clean seam: 20260713 carries d_gw_cdd h0 = +0.435, one of the larger deltas in g23, against a level difference of -0.778 in the OPPOSITE direction. Mean |h0 run delta| on the two clean seams is 0.327 against 0.251 on the sixteen intra-week days of g22/g23 - the seam deltas are if anything LARGER, not structurally zero. (2) The two quantities are not comparable by construction: the run delta compares the SAME target date across two runs, while 'D0 vs the prior session's D0' compares DIFFERENT target dates. They measure different things, so they should disagree everywhere, which is what the falsifier trips over below.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: PARTLY. The seam instance is arithmetic and reproduces, so it could have failed to reproduce and did not. But the claim as a whole cannot be scored against any market outcome, and the one empirical part of it - that the delta channel is structurally near-zero across a seam - was NOT tested against the corpus before merging: the record cites one seam (0629) and one intra-week day (0624), and the second clean seam in the same corpus (0713) goes the other way.

B executed the level rule by hand and derived the sign pre-tape

audits.condition_can_change_state: THE TRIGGER IS A CALENDAR FACT, SO IT CHANGES STATE ON SCHEDULE: 'any weekend or holiday seam' fires on 12 of the 60 days in g18-g23 (every Monday) plus holidays - about 20%, well-behaved. The instrument it governs also moves: d_gw_cdd h0 is served on all twenty days of g22/g23 and ranges -0.500 to +1.053. So there is no degeneracy problem here. The problem is the opposite one - the rule has no outcome attached, so 'can it change state' does not decide usability the way it does for the other nine plays in this batch.
audits.falsifier: WRITTEN AND IT FIRES AGAINST THE PLAY: 'an intra-week day where the run delta and the level difference disagree (they should not - the claim is scoped to seams)'. I ran it on the sixteen intra-week days of g22 and g23 where both channels are served. The two disagree in SIGN on five of sixteen (0624, 0625, 0707, 0710, 0716) and differ by more than 5x in magnitude on seven more. On the play's own text that is five refutations in two blocks. The underlying reason is structural rather than empirical - the run delta compares one target date across two runs while the level difference compares two target dates in one run, so they are not the same quantity and have no reason to agree on any day. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: restate the claim as an arithmetic property of the FEED (how many model cycles elapse across a seam, and whether the served run_delta baselines against the last pre-seam run or the immediately prior run) and verify it against weather_forecast_cycle.max_cycle_runtime_utc, which is served. That is checkable and would either establish the mechanism or dispose of it in one pass.

audits.the_argument: A genuine microstructure mechanism, argued rather than asserted: a phase that prices materially on near-zero net flow is a liquidity VOID - the resting side withdrew rather than size changing hands - so price is DISCOVERING where liquidity actually sits; once found, flow stops moving price and the impact coefficient collapses in both directions. The play is careful about what it claims: 'SEQUENCE claimed; DURATION explicitly NOT claimed', and the reason given is honest (g20's collapse lasted one session, g23's four). ITS ARCHETYPE REPRODUCES TO THE UNIT from g23_mbo_evidence.json: 20260709 phase 2 shows sflow -11, pxchg -1,860, vol 98,400 - the record's 'phase 2 fell -1,860 on -11 net flow across 98,400 lots' exactly. So does C-0715's mirror: 0715 phases 2+3 sum to sflow +6,210 on 68,115 lots for a price change of -80, against the record's '+6,210 net across 68,115 lots for -80'. So do all four post-void pairs: total_sflow +3,747 / +6,326 / +1,089 / +1,333 producing day moves +200 / -60 / -20 / +180. And the g20 second instance is real: 20260529 phase 3 shows sflow -59, pxchg -810, vol 60,930. That is five independent numeric reproductions from a committed evidence file, which is more than most plays in this corpus can offer. WHAT I COULD NOT REPRODUCE, AND IT MATTERS. (1) The k3 triple '0.302 -> 0.026 -> 0.018': the endpoints are recoverable - |day_move| / |total_sflow| gives 0.009 for 0715 (the record's 0.009) and 0.018 for 0716 (the record's 0.018) - but 0.302 does not appear at either the session or the US-phase grain, and the record states no k3 definition. (2) 'the void-signature scan across four groups returns EXACTLY TWO instances'. No signature thresholds are recorded. Running a plainly-stated one (phase |sflow| <= 200, |pxchg| >= 300, vol >= 20,000) over the same four groups returns FIVE: g20 0529 ph3, g21 0615 ph2, g22 0624 ph3, g22 0625 ph2, g23 0709 ph2. The three extra ones are not obviously weaker - g22 0625 ph2 (sflow -12 on 70,526 lots for -380) is a tighter flow void than the g20 instance the record does count. (3) The 'within one session' collapse does not hold for g20 on the session-level k3: 0529 k3 is 0.075, the next session 0601 is 0.261 (the fourth-highest in the block), and the collapse to 0.023 arrives on 0602, two sessions later. It may hold on a signed definition, since 0601 moved -990 against +3,796 of buying, but the record does not say.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: IN PRINCIPLE YES - a corpus-wide scan that returns instances NOT followed by a collapse would refute it, and that is the right shape of test. IN PRACTICE THE SELECTION IS NOT AUDITABLE: with no recorded threshold, 'exactly two instances, both followed by a collapse' cannot be distinguished from a threshold chosen so that the two survivors are the two that worked. My re-scan is the reason this matters - it finds three more candidates, and at least one of them (g22 0625 -> 0626, k3 0.264, mid-range for the block) is not followed by a collapse. Publishing the signature would move this play straight to MECHANISM_VERIFIED or refute it, and either is a good outcome.

audits.condition_can_change_state: YES, AND RARELY, WHICH IS WHAT A VOID SHOULD LOOK LIKE. Scanning all 120 phases of g20-g23 with a stated signature (|sflow| <= 200, |pxchg| >= 300, vol >= 20,000) returns 5 phases across 4 groups - about 4% of phases, spread over all four blocks. The inputs are served on every day (tape_conditions phase_signed_flow and the evidence file's phase pxchg), so nothing is masked and the condition is genuinely evaluable. The consequence variable, k3, also varies over two orders of magnitude across g20-g23 (0.000 to 6.849 on the session definition), so a collapse is a real, detectable event rather than a label.
audits.falsifier: WRITTEN AND WELL-FORMED: 'a void followed by an intact impact coefficient in the next session'. That is exactly the right test, and it is unrunnable as stated because neither the void signature nor the k3 definition is recorded. On my own stated signature the falsifier FIRES TWICE - g22 0625 -> 0626 (k3 0.264, mid-range) and g21 0615 -> 0616 (k3 0.171, ordinary). WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, and it is a small job: record the three void thresholds and the k3 formula in the play, then re-run the scan across g17-g23 and publish the full instance list with the next-session k3 beside each one. If the scan still returns two, the play upgrades to MECHANISM_VERIFIED on the spot; if it returns five with three intact, the sequence claim needs narrowing to the largest voids only.

audits.the_argument: Five weekday labels: Wed weak up-lean, Thu storage catalyst + big magnitude, Fri range, Tue strongest-trend/continuation, Mon weekend-gap big mover. The two limbs that carry a real cause - Thu (the EIA weekly print lands Thursday) and Mon (a weekend of information with no trading) - are each already a dedicated brain play (daytype.storage_thursday_magnitude, daytype.monday_weekend_gap), so the content unique to THIS play is exactly the three limbs with no mechanism argued anywhere: Tue continuation, Wed up-lean, Fri range. Its whole support is an outcome tally - G11 5 fires, 3 on side - and that tally reproduces exactly from the committed score file (0120 +700g/+1930a HIT, 0123 +800/+1170 HIT, 0130 +300/+5020 HIT, 0118 +150/-10 MISS, 0127 +300/-260 MISS). The record is honest about what that is worth: confidence held at 0.4, 'always as a secondary frame', 'never the primary caller on any forward block', Monday-as-reversal arm already retired at G7. Every one of the eleven modern corpus citations says the same thing in the specialist's own words - 'secondary frame only', 'inert', 'adds nothing beyond the monday family'.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: The G11 tally could have (0/5 or 5/5 were both reachable) and it came out at chance on n=5. But no test of a MECHANISM was ever run, because none is argued for the three unique limbs. I ran the obvious one the corpus supports: 70 scored days across g17-g23. The direction limbs are dead - Wed 7 up / 7 down, mean -56 USD, so the 'weak up-lean' has no sign; Tue 7 up / 7 down, mean -17, and its mean absolute move 486 is the second SMALLEST of the week, so 'strongest-trend weekday' is refuted on its own terms. The magnitude limbs survive cleanly - Thu mean absolute move 850, the largest by 40 pct; Fri 435, the smallest; Mon carries essentially all of the block's gap (14 Monday gaps span -750 to +1210 against intra-week gaps of 0-20). So the play splits: a usable day-class magnitude descriptor and two refuted direction claims.

audits.condition_can_change_state: The trigger state changes trivially - day of week always varies - but the play emits a call on ALL FIVE weekdays, so it fires 10 of 10 days in every block and never declines. That is the degenerate form with the sign reversed: not 0-of-10, but 10-of-10. Discrimination measured on 70 days g17-g23: the two direction limbs do not split days (Wed 7/7, Tue 7/7); the three magnitude limbs do (Thu 850 vs Fri 435 mean absolute move, Mon owning every gap).
audits.falsifier: NONE WRITTEN. The play's falsifier field is empty. A serviceable one exists and I ran it: on a rolling 40+ scored days, if Wednesday's up-share is not materially above 0.5 and Tuesday's mean absolute move is not materially above the week's median, the direction limbs are dead. On g17-g23 both fail.

audits.the_argument: A demand-led swing sequences: a mature swing (age >= 4) cannot post a consecutive fresh cum-extreme, so a material fresh extreme close is followed by a give-back or hold, then R1 is applied to the give-back's own close for the resume call; a young swing (<= 3 sessions) chains and must not be faded. The mechanism is a real one - a positioning cycle needs a session to reload - and the play states its own boundary as descriptive rather than sharp, names the swing-side asymmetry (supply-led G3 trended instead of alternating), and hands magnitude to other plays rather than inventing one. The evidence is unusually thick and is COUNTED, not narrated: G7 5/5 with dated pairs and dollar moves; young-chain counterexamples listed; a materiality rule derived from a case it would otherwise have gotten wrong (1112 +100 closed INSIDE 1111's range, so not a material extreme, so 1113 extended); G9 post-flip alternation; G10 bounce-never-extended n=4; and G11 scored per-event at 4 fires, 2 on side, with confidence lowered 0.6 -> 0.55 in consequence.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: Yes, repeatedly, and it did. The G11 tally reproduces exactly from the committed score file - 0120 +700g/+1930a HIT, 0128 -1000g/-400a HIT, 0121 -800g against +3820a MISS, 0127 +300g/-260a MISS - i.e. the play's strongest structural call of that week failed and was written up as a failure with a diagnosed cause (the polarity input, not the rhythm). C-0715 then contradicted the YOUNG-swing limb on G23 0708 in a refine posterior and explicitly declined to propose on it at n=1. That is a rule that has been allowed to lose.

audits.condition_can_change_state: On the refine lane, yes and demonstrably: swing age and 'closed at a material fresh extreme' both vary within every block, the play fires on some days and declines on others, and the >= 300 USD materiality bar was itself derived from a case where it flipped the answer. On the BLIND lane, no - chain age and cum-from-anchor are price content the mask removes, and C stands the play down explicitly on G20 0525/0603, G22 0624/0630/0701 and G23 0707. The brain does not say this; the play carries requires 'needs_day_N-1_tape', which is true at the open of a refine run and false under the mask.
audits.falsifier: NONE WRITTEN (falsifier field empty), but the play is de facto falsifiable and has been partly falsified: a mature swing posting two consecutive material fresh extremes, or a young chain that does not chain. G11 0121 is the first kind. A serviceable written form: over a block, count material-fresh-extreme closes and score the next session; two consecutive extensions in a mature chain more than ~30 pct of the time retires the rhythm.

audits.the_argument: A weekend gap is sized by whether the weekend's model cycle delivers a CHANGE at D+2..D+6 (fresh/accelerating shot -> +1500..+2500, and the GAP not the Monday session carries the repricing) or merely carries an already-priced shot (+200..+400). The brain states plainly how the play was built: 'The three under-forecast instances (1020's +2770 day, 0118, 0125) are now attributed to ONE condition rather than three separate misses.' The condition was constructed to absorb three misses and its evidence is the size of those same three gaps. The fresh/priced labels were assigned after the gaps were known - there is no independent measurement anywhere in the record that could have separated them. The reaction corollary is the honest part and it does carry a mechanism (0119's US session netted +550 after a +2100 gap because the catalyst had already been consumed by the gap it followed).
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: No, as constituted. The five cited numbers verify (0118 gap +2100 and 0125 gap +2480 both reproduce from g11_score.json), but verifying a number is not testing a rule when the rule's category label was chosen after seeing it. The discriminating input is DECLARED UNSERVED in the play's own requires field, and A confirmed at G22 that 'the CDD ladder has zero coverage beyond h1 anywhere in the block, which is precisely the input magnitude.weekend_gap_delivery declares it needs'. The two G22 attempts to proxy it from D+0/D+1 failed in OPPOSITE directions on consecutive weekends, which is what a coin does.

audits.condition_can_change_state: NO, on the served state - and the play says so itself. The discriminating read is a change at D+2..D+6 in the weekend model cycle; decision_state carries no weekend cycle and, per A at G22, no CDD coverage beyond h1 anywhere in the block. So the fresh/priced switch cannot be evaluated at all and is decided by narrative. The SIGN arm (open_time_only from the running chain) is unaffected and is fine.
audits.falsifier: NONE WRITTEN. The play needs one and it is easy: once the Sat/Sun 00Z and 12Z ingest lands, pre-register fresh vs priced from the D+2..D+6 delta BEFORE the reopen and score the gap against the two bands. Until that data build exists the arm is not falsifiable, which is the accurate description of its current state.

audits.the_argument: When chain-drift content owns a weekend with a live chain, read the [600..1600] class as a DAY-MOVE budget (gap plus Sunday session together) rather than as a gap quantity; plain regime takes the class bottom, covering regime takes 2x the class mid (~2200), and Session = budget - gap. The framing claim is good and is the play's real content. The RUNG structure is where the support fails. The doubled rung's only instance, 0308 at +2250, comes from the G14 REFINE: the blind that day forecast -750 with the sign wrong by 3000 USD, and the refined v2 pass then wrote +2200 against the +2250 actual. The form was invented in the refine to explain the refine's own predecessor miss, and the brain says as much in its own evidence field - the 0308 'Sunday envelope break' is 'EXPLAINED by the budget form, not declared'. That is honest, and it is also the definition of the class. The plain rung then has the opposite problem: it sits at ~600 while the play's own stated null prior for non-chain-drift Sundays is <= 690. The two are the same number, so the plain rung buys nothing over declining to fire.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: Partly, and the part that could did. The play's declared first forward test ran at G15 0322 and PASSED on the framing claim in the sharpest possible way: budget called -600, delivered -640, while the gap was called -400 and delivered +290 - gap_dir_ok false. The companion Sunday 0315 repeated it exactly (-450 called, -430 delivered, gap -300 called, +480 delivered). Two Sundays where the total was right to within 40 USD and the split was inverted both times is real evidence that the day-move is the stable object. But it is evidence for the FRAMING, not for the rungs, and neither number distinguishes the plain rung from the <= 690 prior. The doubled rung has never fired again in the walk.

audits.the_argument: A Friday that closes at an extreme cum-from-anchor or on a mature chain (age >= 4) is exhausted rather than continuing, so the weekend is give-back-biased and Monday must not extend it; size the weekend from the give-back class. The mechanism is exhaustion physics and the play declares its own overlap with post_parabolic_bleed and crash_regime_bands rather than pretending to be new - this is the Friday-close-into-weekend instance of the same object, framed for the handoff, which is a legitimate reason for a separate entry. But the merged support is three retrospective Friday-to-Monday day-net pairs assembled in the S104 Friday cleanup specifically to explain Monday misses (0130 +4990 -> 0201 -7590 with 0202 'wrongly EXTENDED +1300, actual -4260'; 1212 -1190 -> 1215 -1570; 0102 -> 0105 +270). The evidence IS the misses. Nothing independent of the outcome was measured, and the forward_evidence field says 'NONE - proposed S104; G17+ is the forward test'.

audits.the_argument: At any session close where last-hour price DIRECTION and last-hour SIGNED FLOW disagree, the flow side owns the next session's bias: price down with flow positive reads as covering or buy-absorption building and biases the next session UP; price up with flow negative reads as distribution and biases it down. The play is careful about its own status - 'a boundary tell, not an owner', never front-run a flip on it alone - and it carries a recorded assumption-retirement from G20 0604 admitting it would flip 0605 to UP and lose 1,350. But its support is two G15 readings whose OUTCOMES are the evidence, and forward_evidence is 'NONE'.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: The merged n=2 could not, and one of the two does not even say what the brain says it says. The 0315->0316 instance is cited as confirming - and 0316 delivered -540, a DOWN day, against a play that calls price-down-with-flow-positive UP. B's posterior credits an INTRA-SESSION phase ('Monday ph2 ACCOMMODATES'), not the next-session direction the play states. The mechanism was read off a sub-object while the stated call was wrong on the day. So I measured the rule as written on the only instrument that serves both fields, the stage-time exit states, across every consecutive-day boundary in G20-G23: it fires on 13 of 36 boundaries and the next day's sign matches the flow side on 5 of 13 (identical 5/13 scoring session-only from the evidence files). Worse than the coin it replaces, on four groups the brain has never looked at. My 5/13 independently reproduces the one failure the brain already records (0604 -> 0605, MISS).

audits.the_argument: Per phase, flow_conviction = sign(signed_flow) * sign(price_change); ALIGNED (>0) delivers the band in the FLOW direction, NEGATIVE (<0) means flow was absorbed against price so the move reverses in the PRICE direction. Absorption is a real microstructure object and the play is right that it matters. But the two branches emit the SAME SIGN. Aligned means the two agree, so 'the flow direction' IS the price direction; negative means they disagree, and the call is explicitly the price direction. Whatever the conviction field reads, the output is sign(price_change). I verified this mechanically on all 70 sessions of g17-g23 from the committed evidence files: at ph2 the emitted sign equals the phase price direction 70 of 70 times, and at the max-volume phase 70 of 70. Support is then a day-net tally - 'flow_conviction called 10/10 signs on G19', n_days 10 - which is the OUTCOME_CREDITED shape, and which does not reproduce: applied as written it scores 8 of 10 on G19 at ph2 and 8 of 10 at the max-volume phase. Something other than the play got the last two. Confidence 0.86.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: The 10/10 could have come out lower - and mechanically it does (8/10). But the DISCRIMINATING claim cannot be tested at all, because aligned and negative phases never disagree about the sign, so no arrangement of outcomes can separate them. Across g17-g23 the rule as written scores 81.4 pct at ph2 and 84.3 pct at the max-volume phase on the day sign, splitting 38 aligned / 32 negative at ph2 with near-identical hit rates (31/38 vs 26/32) - i.e. the conviction label carries no lift over 'the dominant phase's price direction wins'. To the brain's credit, the record already contains the antidote for the OTHER arm: B's adjudication shows the final-phase arm's 4-of-4 rests on a confound (all four G20 exemplars carry negative ph3 flow, so A's and D's opposite readings are observationally identical on 4 of 4), that 24 of 24 intra-week boundaries carry |gap| <= 10 'identically zero by market structure' so D scoped the arm on eight vacuous cases, that both readings go 2/4 on the four scorable weekend seams, and it is filed UNRESOLVED with no scope change merged. That is exactly the discipline the core arm never got.

audits.the_argument: When both aggressor sides fight to a draw at MAXIMUM volume and price still travels, the travel belongs to the resting book, not to either aggressor - conviction UNDEFINED BY CANCELLATION rather than by absence. Two mandatory limbs: (a) final-phase |net| below ~5 pct of the prior phase's, AND (b) final-phase volume at or above the session maximum. This is a genuinely argued mechanism with a named first instance, a written falsifier, and - unusually - a documented adversarial history: it was proposed as FLOWLESS_BID_WITHDRAWAL, B refuted the name and the participation reading, E conceded the fact and rejected the consequence, and the merged form is the conjunction the two ledgers reconcile to. Limb (b) is declared mandatory with the reason stated ('without it the play is a false-positive machine - B's actual objection') and the note that it runs OPPOSITE to what 'flowless' implies. Status PROPOSED, n=1, honestly labelled.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: Yes on the founding instance, which is why this is not OUTCOME_CREDITED: the claim is that an incomplete transfer is RECOVERED at the next seam, and the recovery is a separate, later, independent observation. It could simply not have recovered. G20 0529 ph3 verifies to the digit against the committed evidence file (sflow -59 against ph2's -1,573, vol 60,930 = session max and +18 pct over ph2, pxchg -810) and the 0601 gap verifies at +690 against the actual file, i.e. 85 pct of the travel recovered before a Monday session traded. And the play has been repeatedly tested since, hardest by its own author: E ran limb (a) on complete G21 data and reported '0/10 on limb (a) across the block', including on the 0611 exit its blind had wanted it for ('this is the finding I filed against my own play coming back clean'). C, B and D each measured it failing on named G22 and G23 days with the arithmetic shown. My own sweep confirms the rate: the conjunction fires 1 of 70 sessions across g17-g23 - the founding instance and nothing else.

audits.the_argument: A COHERENT multi-horizon revision on the season's demand axis (all reachable horizons revised the same way) owns the weekend seam's SIGN; positioning does not sign a seam and is a sign-agnostic GAIN term. There is a real mechanism here and one genuinely falsifiable component: reopen participation was tested and refuted in BOTH directions (252 lots produced +1,210 while a 194-trade stub produced +50), which is a rival explanation killed on measurement. But the SIGN claim rests on three seams measured retrospectively inside the single session that proposed it, and one of the three is credited generously - 0628, described as 'largest add', delivered a +50 gap and is booked as 'sign right, size inverted' when +50 is indistinguishable from zero. All three verify against the actuals (0615 -750, 0622 +1210, 0629 +50), which is not the same as testing them.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: The in-sample 3/3 could have. The point is that it already HAS come out the other way and the brain has not been told. The play's own declared forward test is 'G23's two seams' and both have run: 0706 (weekend CDD run-delta +0.963, coherent add across GFS/NAM/MEX, B forecast gap +400) gapped -580; 0713 (run-delta +0.435, coherent multi-horizon add, B forecast gap +400 again) gapped -360. B's refine posterior states the verdict without hedging: 'Both of the g23 Mondays I own had a positive weekend CDD run-delta and both gapped DOWN, and I forecast a +400 up-gap on both. The revision's SIZE class survives; the revision's SIGN rule does not.' Across all five measured seams the sign rule is 2 clean hits, 1 near-zero, 2 clean misses - and the two out-of-sample ones are both misses. The brain still reads status PROPOSED, evidence '3/3 measured seams', forward 'forward test G23's two seams'.

audits.the_argument: A phase whose price moves materially on near-zero net signed flow is a WITHDRAWN BOOK, not absorption. Nothing was transferred, so the level was never tested and tends to be pressed again; true absorption is size CHANGING HANDS against price - flow present, price refusing - and the two objects are opposite and must not share a label. A withdrawn book CONTINUES, an absent book ROUND-TRIPS. The mechanism is argued from price formation rather than from the outcome, and the requires field already carries the correction that separating the two objects needs TWO axes (flow intensity AND price efficiency), not one signature.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: Yes, and the record is a small model of how this should be done. The founding instance verifies to the digit (0709 ph2: sflow -11 on 98,400 lots, pxchg -1,860, the block's largest phase move; ph3 the classic absorption form at +1,390 buying purchasing -160, ph_absorb TRUE) and its consequence is a separate later observation that could have failed - the level was pressed twice more, 0710 -660 and 0713 -620, both verified in the actual file. Then three independent falsification attempts, all reported: (i) E-0717 found its own proposal AS WRITTEN would have labelled its own thin overnight a continuation signal and repaired it into the two-axis form, with both types measured (0709 ph2 at 0.011 pct intensity / 18.9 USD per 1k lots / 63.4 pct of volume = withdrawn book, continuation; 0717 ph1 at 3.43 pct / 140.1 USD per 1k, the block maximum and 3x the next / 5.5 pct = absent book, round trip); (ii) B-0713 supplied the counter-object from the same block - 0713 ph2, |sflow| 158 on 53,859 lots, price -50, impact 0.32 USD per lot against 0709's 169, 'same signature, 530x apart in price response, opposite consequences' - which is what forced a THRESHOLD instead of a signature; (iii) the blind-available discriminator was tested and reported NULL, l1_book.quote_bid_share scoring 6/10 in-block and, per C-0715, 9 fires / 4 hits across G21-G23 with the cause diagnosed (session mean spans 0.475-0.512 while its own intraday p25/p75 is [0.333, 0.667], so aggregation destroys it). An honest negative attached to a proposal is the opposite of the S108 signature.

audits.the_argument: MECHANISM ARGUED, from a validated lineage. The S36/S37 dipole architecture splits turn detection into a FILTER (divergence) and TIMING (fine-resolution price reversal); the exhaustion arm says the imbalance COLLAPSING toward 0.5 marks the leader weakening, and that the collapse - not the crossing - is the signal. That was measured on crypto and then ported to NG futures directly in S90. ONE NAMED MEASUREMENT: on a single NG trend day 2025-07-17 at 1-second bins, oppose+exhaust 0.410 against trend+strengthen 0.382, a +2.7pp right-signed pulse. Recorded with both cell values and a date in research/kalshi/FORECAST_ARCHITECTURE_S111.md and research/kalshi/OPEN_ITEMS.json A-6. THE HONEST LIMIT, and the brain states it itself: forward_evidence NONE, status HYPOTHESIS, confidence 0.25, requires needs_intraday_reveal, scope EXECUTION-layer turn timing and explicitly never a blind open-time curve input. The 2025-07-17 tape predates the walk (the corpus starts 2025-09-08), so the instance cannot be traced to a posterior or an actual - only to two committed research documents that name the date and the numbers. It is not ASSERTED: there is a real mechanism from a lineage that was validated per-cell, and a real measurement with both arms printed. audits.the_argument: MECHANISM: a terminal give-back runs back toward the price level where the swing began and stabilizes there, because below that shelf price is no longer priced by the driver that produced the swing. The squeeze form spells the mechanism out fully - post-expiry appreciation has no delivery anchor and no sponsor, so it unwinds to where the pull began and stops. MEASUREMENT, and this is the strongest instance record in the batch: five per-event instances with dates and dollar outcomes, every one of which I recomputed from the committed continuous series rather than trusting the brain. 0922 close 2.801 -> 0923 2.864 = +630 (brain says +610). 1016 2.925 -> 1017 3.000 = +750 (brain +740). 1117 4.339 -> 1118 4.366 = +270 (brain +270) and the brain names the shelf as the 4.32-4.34 zone, which the 4.339 close sits ON. 1029 3.803 -> 1030 4.062 = +2590 (brain +2580). 1125 4.474 -> 1126 4.611 = +1370 (brain +1360). THE PLAY THEN RECORDS ITS OWN FALSIFICATION AND SCOPES IT: 1211 broke through the 4.367 origin (1210 4.616 -> 1211 4.220) and the brain converts that into a VOID CONDITION - after a confirmed parabolic polarity flip the shelf breaks and the break confirms reversal-not-give-back. n=1 break against n=5 holds, and the discriminator (squeeze form holds / weather-parabola form breaks) is named rather than the tent widened. A play that recorded its own counterexample and derived a condition from it is not resting on outcome credit.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: YES, demonstrably - it DID come out the other way once and the record says so. 1117 could have kept falling through 4.32 and did not; 1211 did fall through 4.367 and was recorded as a void rather than explained away. The added S110 arm (a covering leg retraces in full to its origin only if no phase was validated by aligned flow) is weaker: n=2 clean on the two days its author owned, with 0601 a declared partial where the origin did NOT hold as a floor, and both measured in refine round 2 with the outcome known.

audits.the_argument: TWO DIFFERENT OBJECTS UNDER ONE ID, and they do not share a support class. (1) THE OWNERSHIP LADDER - anchor_structural > positioning_saturation_turn > weekend_cycle_weather > chain_drift - is a genuine decision procedure and it has real forward evidence of correct DECLINES: on G22 0629 both A and B walked the rungs against measured quantities and declined the structural rung on a MEASURED absence (calendar_front_next_spread -0.043 with the front CHEAPENING into its own expiry plus contango on every day of the block - a stranded-premium unwind cannot coexist with a widening contango). That is a rung that could have fired and did not, for a stated reason. (2) THE MAGNITUDE BANDS are the problem, and they are OUTCOME_CREDITED in the strict sense. The evidence is a per-gap back-check table covering EVERY material gap in the walk in which every single actual lands IN its class band - 12 for 12, then 13 for 13 once the s101_6 weather ladder is added, with the file's own note reading 'zero gaps outside their class band' and 'zero re-classifications outside band'. The bands were defined FROM those gaps. A back-check that cannot produce a miss is not a test. The dead-sponsor sizing rule is the honourable exception: it argues a real mechanism, declares n=1 outright, and points at its eleven non-firings as the discriminator - that is a rule with a genuine negative population. But the weather rung, which is the rung that actually owns most gaps, has no such control.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: NOT AS RECORDED - the back-check is in-sample and 13/13 by construction. It HAS come out the other way on the two genuine out-of-sample tests, and both failed on magnitude: G22 0629 (+480 called, +50 delivered) and G23 0713 (+400 called, -360 delivered, sign wrong too). The play's own user retracted the bands mid-corpus - B on 0706 stood the whole play down with 'winter weather bands scope-retracted for summer', which is an in-corpus admission that the bands do not transfer.

audits.condition_can_change_state: THE LADDER YES, THE BANDS NO IN SUMMER. The ownership rungs genuinely change state: structural declined 4/4 forward on G13+G14 and again on G22 0629 and G23 0706/0713 on measured spread and contango; the weather rung owned 0629 and the priced arm owned 0713. But the band VALUES are the degenerate part - +1500..+2500 for a fresh shot is 2.4 to 4.1 sigma against a served n0_net_sigma_10 of 614 and n0_range_pctile 18.3, so A and B both had to rescale the bands by hand before using them, and B eventually retracted them outright. audits.the_argument: MECHANISM, one line and plausible: longs trim spent premium into the weekly close because the driver has realized and the closure is the risk horizon, so a Friday with a stretched same-side chain runs COUNTER-chain after the morning. THE SUPPORT IS FOUR OR FIVE FRIDAYS THAT WENT COUNTER-CHAIN AND WERE NOT CALLED. The brain's own wording gives it away - the play 'promotes the Friday-bag terminal-squaring lean (was n=2 lean) to a conditional rule after two consecutive unapplied hits'. UNAPPLIED. 0227 and 0313 are both rows in E's own miss table: on 0227 the blind called -500 and the day did +350; on 0313 the blind called +300 and the day did -1010. Both verify exactly against the committed record. The rule was written to explain days the forecaster had already missed, and the mechanism was read off the direction those days took. THEN THE TRIGGER WAS TIGHTENED AROUND ITS OWN FAILURE. On G15 0327 the blind fired the play - the posterior says in terms 'TRIGGER NOT met, but its components are ... CREST-FORM LITE ... (FORWARD TEST, partial-trigger form declared)' - and called -350 into a +1150 day. The brain's resolution is that the trigger was never met, and it adds a discriminator (stretched same-side chain AND driver realizing by the close) that excludes 0327 by construction. That may well be right, but it is a condition added after the miss, and the 3/3 crest SHAPE it preserves is the same in-sample three days.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: NO, as constituted. The instances are days selected because they moved counter-chain; there is no recorded population of qualifying Fridays that did NOT trim. The one genuine forward test in the corpus - 0327 - came out the other way, and the response was a narrower trigger rather than a scoping of the claim. The added discriminator has itself never been exercised positively.

audits.condition_can_change_state: NO, NOT IN THE MODERN CORPUS - THIS IS THE CLEAREST DEGENERATE CONDITION IN THE BATCH. I classified every mention across forecasts/ by whether it sat in a plays_fired or a stand-down field. TWO fires in the entire corpus, both in research/kalshi/forecasts/grp15.json, one of them the declared 0327 mis-fire. Against that: stand-downs on G20 0529 and 0605, G21, G22 0626 0702 0703, G23 0710 - eight modern Fridays across four groups, 0 fires. The tightened trigger requires a stretched same-side chain AND a driver realizing by the close, and in summer blocks the driver (heat) is almost always the COUNTER-chain driver and always AHEAD across the seam, so the conjunction cannot close. The degenerate-block share is 4-of-4.
audits.falsifier: None recorded. What it needs is the inverse population: qualifying Fridays (stretched same-side chain, driver realizing by the close) that CONTINUED rather than trimmed. Zero such days are named anywhere, which is why the 3/3 shape claim cannot be scored.

audits.the_argument: THE MEASUREMENT IS THE STRONGEST PART AND IT IS REAL. Nine instances across five groups, each carrying the date, the D-1 run, the close-off-extreme, the blind's own call, the actual and the error. I reproduced two of them end to end from the committed record: g15 0318 Wed close 3.223 against 0317 3.033 = +1900 at coff 0.97, then 0319 closed 3.115 = -1080 against a blind call of -800 (grp15.json guessed_net_usd -800); g14 0311 Wed 3.259 against 0310 3.056 = +2030 at coff 1.0, then 0312 closed 3.233 = -260 against a blind call of +900, err 1160 exactly as the brain states. g15 0324 -380 / 0325 +660 against a blind +250 also reproduces. CRUCIALLY IT CARRIES ITS OWN NEGATIVE POPULATION: two named counterexamples at coff 0.90-0.95 that did NOT give back (g8 0126 +1370 coff 0.95 -> +170 flat; g12 0204 +1260 coff 0.93 -> +510 continued up) which is how the >=0.95 bar was located, plus an interaction VOID on the 1st-2nd session of a fresh turn. That is a threshold sited by counterexample rather than by fit. The mechanism itself is thin - the play describes the forecaster's error ('the blind reads a big directional close as MOMENTUM') more than it describes the market - but the sign claim is separated from the size claim honestly: 'the robust decision-time claim is the SIGN ... the counter-move SIZE is variable (-13 to -106 percent) so band it, do not point-forecast'.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: YES. The high-side population is 6 of 6 on a bar that was set by two days which failed it - had 0126 and 0204 sat above 0.95 the rule would have died. The 3 low-side instances are weaker (all three OVER-sized the bounce, so the rule's direction held while its magnitude did not, and the brain says so). What is missing is a survey of ALL coff>=0.95 days in the corpus rather than the ones that were missed, so the true denominator is unknown.
