audits.condition_can_change_state: NO IN G20-G23, AND IT IS THE ABSOLUTE BARS. Classified every corpus mention: ZERO fires and about twenty-one stand-downs across G20-G23. Two distinct causes and both matter. In the BLIND the limbs are price content and unevaluable - grp23_C_20260708 says 'run-size/close-extreme limbs PRICE-based and masked; unevaluable, declared rather than guessed'. In the REFINE, where price IS available, it is evaluated and comes out NEGATIVE every time: G20 0525 (+270 coff 0.48), G20 0527 (chain age 0 coff 0.06), G20 (coff 0.52), G21 0616 (+970 coff 0.90 - a double near-miss), G22 0630 (+790 coff 0.56), G23 0707 (0.11 off the LOW). The >=1200 USD bar was calibrated on winter and shoulder blocks whose realized moves ran ~800; the summer blocks run ~460, so the bar now sits in the tail of its own distribution. This is D23's disease with the D23 remedy: the bar needs re-siting at the CENTRE of the live distribution, not converting to a percentile.
audits.falsifier: None in the falsifier field. The counterexample_and_scope block is effectively one - a coff>=0.95 day with a >=1200 run and chain age >=2 that CONTINUES would kill the high-side arm - and the boundary band 0.90-0.94 is already declared unclean rather than claimed.

audits.the_argument: THIS IS A MEASURED SELF-DIAGNOSIS, NOT A MARKET CLAIM, AND IT SHOULD BE READ AS ONE. Its evidence is E's Friday self-analysis: an eighteen-row miss table with group, guess, actual, direction hit and a failure mode per row, summing to 28,580 USD of Friday error, of which 13 rows (72 percent) collapse to one root - the Friday sign was taken from a day-class default or a chain extrapolation instead of from the turn/exhaustion state already sitting in decision_state. I verified three rows exactly against the committed record: 0227 g13 guess -500 actual +350 (grp13.json guessed_net_usd -500; g13 closes 2.822 -> 2.857); 0327 g15 guess -350 actual +1150; 0313 g14 guess +300 actual -1010. The prescription follows from the diagnosis rather than from a market regularity - run the turn check FIRST and forbid the prior as the direction source - and the file is careful about what is free and what is not: every wrong SIGN was reasoning with the information present, only the magnitude tail (3 MHS + 1 DAT) is data-limited. THE HONEST SPLIT: the diagnostic half is measured and reproducible; the market half - 'if the exhaustion/turn signals fire, the Friday sign is the TURN direction' - has n=1 forward (0417 flipped to covering-UP correctly, on a +40 day where direction is a scoring artifact) and has never returned a TURN verdict in a modern blind.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: PARTLY. The 13/18 concentration could have come out heterogeneous - the file explicitly asks 'is it the SAME flaw, or a different one every time' and reports a histogram with five other modes that could have dominated. That is falsifiable. What is NOT independently checkable is the mode LABEL on each row: those are self-assigned ('one failure mode each, my judgment'), so a reader cannot re-derive 13/18 without re-adjudicating eighteen days. And the prescription's own arm is untested: three modern blind Fridays and the gate returned CLEAN, CLEAN and NOT-CLEAN-but-no-turn - it has never actually flipped a sign in a scored blind.

audits.condition_can_change_state: THE TRIGGER IS UNCONDITIONAL BY DESIGN (any Friday, before a sign is emitted) so the thing that must change state is the VERDICT, and it barely does. Measured across the modern blind Fridays: 0626 CLEAN, 0710 CLEAN, 0703 NOT-CLEAN-but-no-turn. Zero TURN verdicts in G22/G23, and the only recorded flip in the whole corpus is the G17 0417 test-drive on a +40 day. The individual limbs vary properly (chain age 2 vs 4-5, cum at extreme vs not, positioning 29.25 pctile vs extreme) so the gate is not reading a frozen field - but the composite has not yet produced the output that would distinguish it from 'do not use a day-class default'.
audits.falsifier: None in the falsifier field. A usable one: a Friday where the exhaustion limbs fire and the day continues with the chain anyway. Also worth noting the play's own caveat already carves out one class (the 0327-type mechanical settle-spent covering close) as wrong-signed but self-limiting, which is a scope limit rather than a falsifier.

audits.the_argument: THIS IS THE S108 SIGNATURE AND IT IS ALMOST TEXTBOOK. The whole evidence field reads: 'g19: both EIA prints were blind-wrong-signed by reading absorption as a damp; as a reversal both flip correct (0514 +450 vs +590, 0521 -400 vs -420)'. I verified the setup - grp19.json has 0514 blind -150 against +590 actual and 0521 blind +280 against -420 actual, both wrong-signed - so the factual claim is accurate. But the inference is exactly the one the audit exists to catch: two days whose outcomes were known were re-read with the flag inverted, both then agreed, and the inverted reading was merged as a general mechanism scoped to ALL day-classes at confidence 0.85. n_days is given as 4 with only 2 named. Nothing was tested against a population. The one piece of forward evidence in the record is honest about being something else entirely - the g20_0528 entry ends 'This is the play working as a check on a specialist, not on the market.' I RAN THE POPULATION TEST because the flags are served in every g17-g23 evidence file. D-1 session absorption predicting the next day's sign: 11/22 across seven groups. Absorbed phase k predicting phase k+1 against the absorbed side: 11/25. Final-phase absorption predicting the next day: 14/22 against a 36/69 up base rate. The only slice that clears is the EIA-print subset the exemplars were drawn from: 4/6 (0430 and 0611 miss; 0514 0521 0528 0604 hit). Method declared: absorbed side taken from total_sflow sign on days with absorb_session true, which may be stricter or looser than a specialist's reading, and I am reporting it as an audit signal not a verdict.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: NO as recorded - inverting a reading on two days you already know the answer to cannot fail. It CAN come out the other way when run against the served flags, and it largely does: 11/22 and 11/25 are coin flips, and the play's stated scope ('all day-classes incl EIA print days') is the part that does not survive while the EIA subset it was born on does.

audits.condition_can_change_state: YES, HEALTHILY - this is not a degenerate condition, it is a non-discriminating one. absorb_session reads true on 24 of 70 days across g17-g23 (34 percent) and ph_absorb fires on 25 phase-transitions, so the trigger splits days properly within every block. The problem is downstream: when it fires, the outcome it predicts arrives at roughly the base rate. Separately, grp23_state_audit.json names this play as affected by finding f3 - vol_regime's n0 basis carries only 22.6 percent of the scored leg's tape in G23 (2,594 against 11,501) - which degrades the magnitude side of any absorption sizing in that era, though not the direction flags themselves.
audits.falsifier: None in the falsifier field, which is itself the defect - a play at confidence 0.85 scoped to all day-classes with no stated way to lose. The obvious one: absorbed sessions where the following session goes with the absorbed side at better than chance. On the served flags that is currently 11 of 22.

audits.the_argument: AN ARGUED MECHANISM WITH ONE TRACED INSTANCE, CORRECTLY LABELLED - and then a repair that does not do what it claims. The mechanism is stated and non-trivial: when participation falls, price per unit of flow rises roughly as fast, so excursions survive even though the net does not, and scaling BOTH halves by sqrt(participation) is wrong on the range half. The first instance is measured, not asserted: G20 0525 Memorial Day, which I recomputed from the evidence file - n_trades 12,477 against a block mean of 44,648 (28 percent participation) and a realized range of 1,140 against the served n0_range_20_mean of 1,094, i.e. 1.04x rather than the ~0.55x sqrt-scaling predicts. Its author also withdrew its own round-1 characterisation of the excursion as 'a reactive tail' in favour of a mechanism (a deadline-bound roll-in buyer facing a 13:00 early close). That is NOVEL_N1 done properly. THEN IT WAS REFUTED ON ITS FIRST FORWARD TEST BY ITS OWN AUTHOR - G21 0619 Juneteenth, realized range 700 which I confirm is sqrt(10,006/36,676) x 1,278 = 695 - and the brain records the refutation, the downgrade and the instruction not to extrapolate. Exemplary. THE PROBLEM IS THE S110 REPAIR. It offers a taxonomy (volume-bound programs preserve range, risk-bound participants do not) and credits it with 'sqrt(participation) survives its second consecutive forward pass - net 410 vs 453 predicted on 0703'. That is a pass on the NET half, which the play never disputed. On the RANGE half 0703 compressed too: n_trades 11,501 against a 37,557 block mean gives sqrt = 0.553 and 0.553 x 1,140 = 630 against a realized 690. So the headline claim is now 1 for 3 and the record cites the third instance as support.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: YES ON EVERY COUNT, WHICH IS WHY THIS RECORD IS WORTH KEEPING. 0525's range could have come in at 600 and did not; 0619's could have come in at 1,200 and did not; both are recorded with the same candour. The failure is not the evidence, it is the credit assignment on the repair - and the repair's discriminator does not separate the two instances (see condition field).

instances.what_the_state_said: Memorial Day partial session at 12,477 trades against a 44,648 block mean (28 percent) with a served n0_range_20_mean of 1,094 and a healthy n0 store (n0_prev_trades 42,233 on 0522) so the benchmark is sound.
instances.what_the_day_did: Realized range 1,140 (high_exc +860 low_exc -280) = 1.04x the mean against a sqrt-predicted ~0.55x, while the net came in at +270 - net compressed, range did not. The founding instance, and it reproduces.

instances.what_the_state_said: Juneteenth partial at 10,006 trades against a 36,676 block mean (27.3 percent). A had predicted range invariance in its blind and then withdrew it in refine under the key MY_OWN_RANGE_PREDICTION_REFUTED_AND_WITHDRAWN.
instances.what_the_day_did: Realized range 700 (high_exc +440 low_exc -260) against sqrt(0.273) x 1,278 = 695. The sqrt scaling the play forbids held to within 5 dollars.

instances.what_the_state_said: The S110 participant_taxonomy note credits 0703 as the play's 'second consecutive forward pass' on sqrt(participation) - net 410 against 453 predicted.
instances.what_the_day_did: Actual net +410 so the NET claim passes. But realized range was 690 (11,501 trades against a 37,557 block mean, sqrt-predicted 630) - the RANGE compressed roughly as sqrt for the second time running. The pass is on the half of the claim that was never in dispute.

audits.condition_can_change_state: THE REPAIR'S DISCRIMINATOR CANNOT SEPARATE THE PLAY'S OWN TWO INSTANCES, AND I CHECKED THE SERVED FIELDS. The repair says invariance needs a DEADLINE-BOUND participant, and A verified in_bcom_roll and in_gsci_roll both FALSE on 0619 as the reason it failed. But I pulled flow_calendar for 0525 as well and in_bcom_roll, in_gsci_roll, in_bidweek, is_expiry_day and is_opex_day are ALL FALSE there too - identical to 0619. So on the served flags the supporting instance and the refuting instance are indistinguishable, and the 'deadline-bound roll-in buyer' on 0525 is asserted rather than measured. The flags themselves are fine as fields (in_bcom_roll and in_gsci_roll true on 15 of 60 days across g18-g23, in_bidweek 14, expiry and opex 3 each) - they simply do not fire on either thin day. SECOND CAVEAT: grp23_state_audit.json finding f3 names this play directly - vol_regime's n0 store carries 22-27 percent of the scored leg in G22/G23, so a participation read in that era sees a quarter of the real tape. G20 and G21 are clean (n0_prev_trades 42,233 and 41,294) so the two founding measurements are unaffected.
audits.falsifier: None in the falsifier field, but the play effectively supplied one and it fired: a thin session whose range compresses as sqrt(participation). That is now 0619 and, on my recomputation, 0703. The taxonomy repair needs its own - a VOLUME-BOUND thin session (roll, bidweek, expiry or opex flag actually true) whose range compresses as sqrt anyway. No such day has been tested.

audits.the_argument: A NEGATIVE RESULT, MEASURED TWICE IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES IT REAL. The claim is that the weekend gap is not ownable as a POINT from current instruments, and the support is two committed point calls that missed in opposite directions - 0622 forecast +20 against +1,210 actual, 0629 forecast +480 against +50 actual. I traced both to the posteriors that emitted them (grp22_B_20260622.json overnight_gap_usd 20; grp22_B_20260629.json overnight_gap_usd 480) and both actuals to g22_actual.json. The decomposition claim also reproduces exactly: on 0622 the SESSION read was sound while the gap was not - B called gap +20 net -420 so session -440, against actual gap +1,210 day +650 so session -560, session error 120 against gap error 1,190, precisely as the brain states. A third supporting measurement is that add-size did not sort gap-size (inverted across 0621/0628). THEN THE PLAY MEASURED ITS OWN EMISSION FORM AND FOUND IT WANTING, which is the mark of a live rule: the S110 note on 0706 records gap +400 against -580 (sign wrong, err 980) plus session +100 against +680 (err 580) hidden behind a day-level score of 400, and draws the right conclusion - 'a wide band that cannot straddle zero is a fuzzy point', and D4 applies INSIDE a day between the gap and the session. WHAT THE BRAIN DOES NOT CARRY: 0713, where the same specialist emitted +400 with a band of +50..+900 against an actual -360. Two G23 seams, two wrong signs, one recorded.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: YES. The two point calls could have landed and the negative would have died; the play even names the condition that would license point emission again ('a block where a pre-committed POINT gap call lands inside +-300 on both Mondays'). And the emission form it prescribes has since been measured against and FAILED on sign, twice, with the first failure written into the play's own record. A rule that publishes the evidence against itself is not resting on outcome credit.

instances.what_the_state_said: B emitted a POINT gap of +20 with a session net of -420 for the block-opening Monday.
instances.what_the_day_did: Actual gap +1,210 and day +650 - so the gap missed by 1,190 while the implied session read (-440 called against -560 realized) missed by 120. The gap and the session are different instruments and the day number hides it.

instances.what_the_state_said: B emitted a POINT gap of +480 (band +200..+850) on a fresh weekend CDD add of +4.7 gw.
instances.what_the_day_did: Actual gap +50. The second point miss and in the opposite direction from 0622, which is what makes the pair a negative result rather than a bias.

instances.what_the_state_said: The prescribed form was used: 'The gap number is a BAND TOKEN not a point claim: band +150..+700 (0.5-1.0x era-degraded sigma ~600 mid-book gain)' with gap +400 and session +100 split for separate scoring.
instances.what_the_day_did: Actual gap -580 and day +100 so session +680. Magnitude right (|580| inside |150..700|) sign wrong; session under by 6.8x. 1,560 of component error behind a day-level score of 400 - the play's own S110 note measures this correctly.

instances.what_the_state_said: Same form again: 'Gap = SIGN UP (coherent weekend add) + WIDE BAND +50..+900 ... point authority refused' with the +400 explicitly a p50 inside the band.
instances.what_the_day_did: Actual gap -360 and day -620. Sign wrong for the second consecutive G23 Monday, and the band again could not straddle zero. THIS INSTANCE IS NOT IN THE BRAIN - the S110 note records only 0706.

audits.condition_can_change_state: MOSTLY YES, WITH ONE UNEXERCISED RUNG. The trigger is unconditional (any weekend or holiday gap) which is appropriate for an emission rule. The one mapped numeric condition - cot.managed_money_net_pctile_3y <= 5.0, which selects the 1.5-2.5x sigma extreme rung - fires on 5 of 60 days across g18-g23 and only in one COT week (G20 week 2, all five days at 2.23 against a range that reaches 41.72 by G23). It therefore CAN change state, but it selected zero of the four modern weekend seams on which the emission form was actually used, so the extreme rung is untested. The mid-book rung has been used four times and, per the play's own S110 finding, the failure is not the width but that the band never spans zero.
audits.falsifier: STATED AND CONCRETE, one of the few in the batch: 'a block where a pre-committed POINT gap call lands inside +-300 on both Mondays (would license point emission again)'. G23 was the designated forward test and it fired the opposite way - both Mondays wrong-signed.

audits.the_argument: THE BEST-EVIDENCED PLAY IN THE BATCH, and it was found the honest way round - discovered on one day and then corpus-searched under D24 rather than asserted. MECHANISM, and it is a real one that makes a distinct prediction: the pre-print run is INVENTORY not conviction, built by desks positioning for the number; the print is the scheduled moment that inventory must be defended; a counter impulse means the people who built it are liquidating, which is why the round-trip OVERSHOOTS rather than stopping at flat. MEASUREMENT: 6/6 across five groups with per-instance numbers published in the proposal - 0416 g17 (pre +420, i60s -50, day +720), 0430 g18 (+320, +250, +1230), 0528 g20 (+890, +290, +2100), 0604 g20 (+960, -110, +1130) continue; 0625 g22 (+340, -420, -60) and 0716 g23 (+560, -480, -20) round-trip. I checked all six day-nets against g17-g23 actuals and every one matches. HORIZON STABILITY IS REPORTED WITH ITS OWN FAILURE: stable at 30s and 120s, DEGRADES at 300s where 0604's -310 would falsely fire - a negative result kept rather than trimmed. THE SYMMETRIC ARM IS REFUSED: on the five Thursdays entering 10:29 with a run of -300 or worse, no 60-second impulse reached |300| at all, so the rule declines to apply and says so. AND THE DEFLATIONARY READING IS NAMED BY THE AUTHOR: 'that this is ordinary first-minute momentum is not excluded by n=6', with 0604 offered as the case that would distinguish it (a mild -110 counter failed to stop a +1130 day, which a momentum rule would have faded). The discovery day corroborates independently in the committed evidence file: 0716's session high printed at 10:29:06 ET, fifty-four seconds before the release, and the print was a BULLISH +41 against a ~45 survey that the market then sold - direct evidence against surprise-sign reasoning.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: YES, and part of it did. The 6/6 sort could have been 3/6; the 300-second horizon DID come out the other way and is recorded; the down-run population could have shown the same sort and did not, so the rule was scoped rather than extended. The unverifiable part, declared: the 60-second impulse values themselves are not in the committed corpus - g23_mbo_evidence.json carries only three phases per day - so I can confirm every outcome and the 10:29:06 high but not the impulses. The +-300 bar also sits in a wide empty gap (-110 to -420), so its exact value is unconstrained by the data.

instances.what_the_state_said: Discovery day. Reopen-to-10:29 delivered +560 and set the session high at 10:29:06 - fifty-four seconds BEFORE the release - then the 60-second impulse was -480.
instances.what_the_day_did: Full round-trip: low at 11:08:53, delivery to -770, three hours of basing, covering rally reclaiming 56 percent, close -20 against a 2.900 open. hi_et and lo_et in the evidence file confirm the timing independently. All three phases flow-ALIGNED with absorb_session FALSE - the near-zero net is cancellation of two convicted legs.

instances.what_the_state_said: Pre-print run +340, 60-second impulse -420 - the rejecting arm.
instances.what_the_day_did: Actual day move -60, a full round-trip of the pre-print run. The second and only other member of the rejecting arm.

instances.what_the_state_said: Pre-print run +960 with a MILD counter impulse of -110 - inside the +-300 confirming band despite pointing down.
instances.what_the_day_did: Actual +1130. This is the load-bearing instance: a plain momentum rule would have faded the counter, and it is also the day that falsely fires at the 300-second horizon, which is why the arbiter is placed inside the first two minutes.

instances.what_the_state_said: Pre-print run +890 with a +290 impulse - inside the band, so continue.
instances.what_the_day_did: Actual +2100, the largest single day in G20 and the largest in the continuing arm.

audits.condition_can_change_state: YES AND IT IS A HEALTHY SPLIT - the best in this batch. There are 14 EIA Thursdays across g17-g23; the trigger (pre-print UP run >= +300) selects 6 of them (43 percent), so it is neither 0-of-N nor N-of-N, and the ledger confirms all 14 were examined rather than 6 cherry-picked ('the pre-print share of day travel has median 49.5 percent, n=14 across 7 groups'). Within the fired population the arbiter itself splits 4 continue / 2 reject. The one caution is that both arms are small and the reject arm is n=2. The input is intraday tape at 60-second resolution around 10:30, which is NOT a blind open-time field - this is an execution-lane instrument like the futures-to-Kalshi lag, and the arbiter is causally inside the day it adjudicates, so it should never be scored as an open-time forecast.
audits.falsifier: STATED AND SHARP: 'a pre-run-up print day where the first-minute impulse points one way and the day resolves the other', refined in the proposal to an impulse at or beyond -300 that still closes materially up, or an impulse inside +-150 that nonetheless round-trips. The play also nominates its own forward test (G24+ EIA Thursdays) and calls its own n thin.
